text:
Nebius is making an interesting bet on the AI boom, which im seeing more ppl consider.

it says it could sell all its 2027 GPU capacity today. but it's deliberately holding some back, betting that customers needing GPUs urgently will pay much higher prices.

seems rational.. gpu rental prices across 6 providers is up 27% from jul-oct.

Nebius also has $12B of dedicated Meta contracts, plus an arrangement for Meta to buy certain unsold capacity. so it's not entirely exposed to spot demand.

but also consider the financing side.
on Oct 17, Nebius signed a $3.5B secured bridge facility that matures in just 364 days. interest starts at SOFR + 2.75%, then steps up 25bps every 90 days, reaching as high as +3.5%.

think about that.

Nebius is keeping some compute capacity available to capture higher short-term prices, while using short-term debt to finance its expansion.

that works beautifully while GPU demand is tight and capital is available.

but i wonder whether Nebius can replace that bridge with cheaper, longer-duration financing before GPU rental prices (potentially) soften? the upside is capturing scarcity pricing. the risk is needing fresh capital when scarcity no longer commands a premium.

That's the trade I'm watching in $NBIS.

author: inversebrah
quoted_text:
In 1941, a Spaniard walked into the British embassy in Madrid and offered to spy on the Nazis.

The British turned him down.

So he went to the Germans instead, pretended to be a loyal fascist, and got hired as a German spy. His plan was to lie to them for the rest of the war.

It worked better than anyone could have imagined.

His name was Juan Pujol García. Before the war he had tried his hand at running a chicken farm and a movie theater. He had no spy training. What he had was a deep hatred of both fascism and communism after the Spanish Civil War, and an incredible imagination.

The Germans gave him a codename, invisible ink, money, and orders to go to Britain and recruit spies.

He didn't go to Britain.

He went to Lisbon, Portugal, and made everything up.

Using a tourist guidebook, maps, magazines, newsreels, and a British railway timetable from the library, he wrote long, detailed reports about life in England. Military movements. Morale. Ports.

He'd never been there. He made mistakes. He didn't understand British money. He once reported that dockworkers in Glasgow would do anything for a liter of wine.

The Germans loved him anyway.

Then British codebreakers reading German messages noticed something strange. The Germans were hunting for a convoy that didn't exist, based on a report from some agent in Britain they'd never heard of.

The British went looking for this mystery spy. They found Pujol. In 1942 they finally took him on and brought him to London.

Now he had real help. MI5 gave him the codename Garbo, after the actress, because they thought he was the greatest actor in the world.

Together with his British handler, Pujol built a fake spy network for the Germans. It eventually had 27 imaginary agents. Each had a name, a personality, a job, and a backstory. A Welsh nationalist. A Venezuelan student. A Greek sailor. Some of them recruited their own imaginary sub-agents.

When they needed to explain why one agent had gone quiet, they killed him off. They even put a fake obituary in a Liverpool newspaper. The Germans reportedly paid a pension to his widow.

Who also didn't exist.

Then came D-Day.

Hours before the landings, the British let Pujol send a message warning the Germans that the invasion was coming in Normandy. It was timed so it would arrive too late to matter, but it made him look brilliant.

Three days later he sent the most important message of his career. Normandy was a trick, he said. The real invasion was still coming, at Calais, led by a huge army under General Patton.

That army was fake too. But the Germans believed him.

German forces that could have been rushed to Normandy were held back near Calais for weeks, waiting for an attack that never came.

The Germans were so grateful they awarded him the Iron Cross.

A few months later, King George VI made him a Member of the Order of the British Empire.

He's one of the only people known to have been decorated by both sides of the war.

After the war, afraid of revenge from surviving Nazis, he faked his own death from malaria in Africa and disappeared to Venezuela, where he lived quietly running a shop.

For decades the world thought he was dead.

In 1984, a British writer tracked him down. Pujol came back to Normandy for the 40th anniversary of D-Day and met veterans who had landed on the beaches.

Some of them thanked him.

author: inversebrah
quoted_text:
This is how you can find hidden cameras (even the ones without lenses) with a few light flashes.

Researchers came up with a surprisingly effective method they call Eye of Sauron. 

Just rapidly switch the lights in a room on and off. When the scene changes abruptly, a camera’s codec has to re-encode a lot of new data, which spikes electromagnetic emissions from its memory controller. If you sync the flashes with an EMI scanner, you can pick up this signature and locate the camera - even pinhole ones that only record to an SD card or stream over a cable.

In their experiment with 50 different camera models, every single one was detected after just four scene changes. Some were found more than 20 meters away and even through walls. Detection range reached ~30 m for plastic-cased cameras and ~11 m for metal ones (far better than typical commercial detectors that only work at 1–2 meters). The whole scan took between 4 and 32 seconds depending on room size.

The method nicely complements classic RF scanning and looking for lens reflections. They also used radio-astronomy filtering techniques to cut through the usual household noise (phones, routers, kettles, etc.).

text:
When the market is thin and rotational, keeping it simple is the edge, so here's how I'm trading these conditions.

- Take fewer trades. Only the A+ idea gets capital and second or third best ideas are how you bleed in chop.

- Hold fewer positions at once. More positions means more attention spread thin and more correlated risk when BTC turns.

- Take profit on alts when they've made a large move and BTC is pushing into resistance. That's usually where the alt bid disappears first.

- Trade your own plan. Don't wait for someone else's TP and SL levels, Market is too reactive, lots of headlines, things change quick.

- Don't assume new money is coming in. Pipe dream we have been preached on for too long already. Nothing confirms it yet so treat this as a rotation game where speed beats conviction.

- Don't buy into strength at the highs. 9/10 it fails unless there's a confirmed breakout with real follow-through.

- Cut fast when the trade is invalidated or Pa is off. In a speed game, hoping is more expensive than being wrong.

- Size down. Smaller positions keep you calm enough to follow your plan and in chop the goal is to compound smaller wins with a linear PnL Curve, not to make it all back on one trade.

- Stick to the main coin and skip the far-fetched beta, in thin liquidity the proxies are the first to dump and the last to bounce.

- Decide whether a trade is a scalp or a swing before you enter, and don't let a failed scalp turn into a hopeful swing.

So it turns out that Ukraine's issues with Starlink were caused by Ukraine.

Starlink terminals disconnected at speeds above 160 KPH, as determined by the Starlink terminals internal GPS.

To get around this, Ukraine hacked the Starlink terminals to think they were stationary regardless of speed.

SpaceX figured this out, and updated the system software to detect excessive speed by seeing how rapidly the terminal switched from on satellite to another.  This broke Ukraine's hack, and Starlink would no longer work at high speeds.

Ukraine was using Starlink in a way that violated the terms of service.

Starlink figured it out and stopped it.

quoted_text:
Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications.

On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments.

While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software.

After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely.

text:
A16Z的加密基金改名，是要离开加密领域了么？Chris Dixon这篇长文也是验证了一年前引用推文里聊的“暴论”：以前所期待的区块链技术能跟很多场景结合，例如游戏、社交、电商甚至很多线下业务结合以期望带来真正的创新落地和价值创造，可能并不存在。区块链最大应用是传业务上链（资产发行、交易、流动融合）和AI Agent间用代币作为激励与交易媒介，核心加密从独立赛道转向链上金融新资本范式的底层基础设施。

所以A16Z将Crypto基金更名为A16Z Frontier，正是因为加密技术已成熟并深度融入传统金融与新兴AI场景，不再适合用单一“Crypto”标签定义，其动作直接验证了“Crypto”边界已扩展为更广泛前沿技术的底层能力。 而SEC推动Project Crypto、传统资产链上迁移及稳定币增长，进一步印证融合趋势加速，

区块链正从“独立赛道”变成更多产品可以直接调用的底层能力，标签的重要性在下降。当华尔街、fintech 和传统机构已经把区块链当作基础设施来用时，再把一家公司简单贴上“crypto 公司”标签就不够用了。Dixon 的原话是，现在更应该根据公司“做什么”而不是“用什么技术”来定义它。

a16z 改名正是为了捕捉这个变化。它不是退出加密，而是扩大范围到“frontier startups”——那些创造新市场、可能需要多年发展的技术公司（包括大量 AI 相关的）。加密仍然是重点投资和监管倡导的对象，但边界已经扩大，因为很多真正有影响力的公司会把区块链当作工具，而不是身份。
author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
结合@divine_economy和@colinwu两位关于加密应用创新乏力的感慨聊聊最近在思考的一个暴论：我们以前所期待的区块链技术能跟很多场景结合，例如游戏、社交、电商甚至很多线下业务结合以期望带来真正的创新落地和价值创造，可能并不存在。区块链技术、代币经济、加密资产未来最大的应用场景并不是所期待的crypto原生的创新应用，而是来自两个场景：
一个是传统web2业务快速往链上迁移，币股融合同权，代币也会享受到真实业务带来的收益和相应权利，因为只有真实有价值创造的业务才能让代币经济正向循环起来，不然所谓的代币经济还是在空转；之前https://t.co/tWslvdeGJH这里有聊过；
二是AI通过crypto货币来激励其他bot、agent甚至激励人类完成要做的事情就顺理成章了，智能合约、分布式账本、代币未来是agent与agent、agent与bot、bot与bot交互的主要途径和媒介，从这个角度看Crypto可能是为未来高度完全数字化社会准备的。之前这里有聊过：https://t.co/EKhEhrrP9I

以前移动互联网创投领域有一个十倍效率提升的说法：只有十倍效率提升用户才会迁移，加密行业发展到现在真正十倍效率提升的就是资产的发行、交易和流动，这些都是天然高效率，也就是我们看到链上交易开始大行其道和稳定币的大发展、这本质上就是一种新的资本范式，更高的资本资产流动带来更高的资本效率。之前聊过https://t.co/5XSa9bN1oW

这也是SEC主席Atkins五月份在代币化加密工作组圆桌会议上的讲到“链上证券也有潜力重塑证券市场包含发行、交易、持有和使用证券的的各个方面。例如，链上证券可通过智能合约实现股息的自动分发。代币化还可增强资本形成，将原本流动性差的资产转变为可交易的投资机会，区块链技术有望拓展证券的多种新用途。”从这个角度出发、加密行业这种新的资本范式跟大量传统web2业务结合，跟未来即将要出来AI agent和bot普及场景相结合，应该能有更大的发展空间。

除了围绕资产发行、交易、流动的创新和创业，其他把区块链技术落地到具体的业务场景上的努力有可能一开始方向就错了。

author: 0xJason
quoted_text:
最近推上聊 @predictdotfun 的人多了不少，很开心能被这么多人看到和了解到。不过有几个点被反复提起，我觉得多少有点误解，这里也和大家讨论下

1️⃣ TVL 为什么没别人高

我们的协议 TVL（OI）长期在 $10M 上下，有三个原因：用户主要交易的是加密货币短时涨跌、体育和电竞比赛这类短周期事件，平均持仓和结算时间都很短；我们的积分基本没往持仓上倾斜；再加上我们直接接入了币安的交易所和钱包，用户拿交易所余额就能下单，钱不用趴在协议里

反观友商之前的高 TVL，大量积分分给了持仓，又没有短期市场，撸毛用户只能拆分仓位长期拿着来刷积分，TVL 自然被推上去了

我自己的看法是，预测市场的 OI 远没有 perps 那么关键。perps 要卷 OI，是因为刷交易量成本太低，光看交易量给分培养不出用户习惯，也转不起增长飞轮，所以才要求大量持仓，预测市场不存在这个问题

2️⃣ 交易量是不是刷分刷出来的

这个误解最大。预测市场最重要的是订单簿流动性，所以我们把大部分积分给了流动性提供者，付手续费拿到的积分并不多。举个例子：现在纯靠刷交易量和手续费拿积分的用户，成本大概 0.3u 一分，而场外某老 x 的最新报价是 0.1u 一分。谁会花三倍的钱在我们这刷量撸分？哈哈哈

3️⃣ 29M 手续费撑不撑得起 1.6B的盘前市值

也有人说我们今年累计手续费 $29M，撑不起盘前 1.6B 的估值。但预测市场这个赛道还在高速增长，还非常早期。Kalshi 这个月的交易量和手续费收入是去年同期的十倍以上，我们现在的单日手续费也是今年一月的十倍多。炒过股的朋友都懂，高成长赛道从来都是给高 PE 倍数来估值的，拿静态收入去算没什么意义

最后再给大家分享两个很有意思的数据也能很好地说明我们在大量虹吸 Polymarket 的市场份额和用户，从下面两张图上可以看到 Crypto 涨跌全市场的交易用户数和交易量总数在过去半年都是变化不大的，但是 Polymarket 的用户数和交易量都在大幅下滑，同时这个下滑数量基本和我们的增长量是一致的，这个说明什么就懂得都懂啦～

有问题欢迎大家在评论区直接问我们哦 @dingalingts @yuexiaoyu @TC8880

text:
Arthur Hayes：高估值垃圾币即使在币安也没有上币效应

Flop Labs CEO Arthur Hayes  @CryptoHayes 10 月 16 日接受 LukeMartin @VentureCoinist  频道采访时表示，整个加密行业都在滥用代币经济学。从早期 ICO 到后来的 VC 私募和代币预售，一些项目方融资后本应开发产品，却在协议上线、代币解锁后抛售持仓，让 TGE 阶段买入的散户承受损失，部分代币跌幅甚至达到 95%。

Hayes 认为，散户已经看穿高 FDV、低流通量代币的套路，这类代币如今连在 Binance 都难以拉升。相比之下，他更看好 Hyperliquid 等具有实际市场需求、将收入回馈代币持有者，且没有大量预售代币解锁抛压的项目。

text:
按这个理论来看，狼崽主动帮飞崽，其实算是一件利人利己的事。表面上是狼崽在帮飞崽，但实际上狼崽也从中获利，因为狼崽也不会随便帮一个没名气的人，本质上是在筛选优质的人去帮。

那这种事是不是应该少做？表面上看似双赢，但其中有两个隐性成本：

一是狼崽没帮过的人和身边的朋友，可能会想「为什么他愿意帮一个不认识的飞崽，却不帮我们？」，心里因此产生嫉妒；

二是以后哪天狼崽不再帮飞崽了，飞崽可能反而会讨厌他。
author: wolfyxbt
quoted_text:
“利他思维”是一种很高级的善意，这一点我在狼崽哥@wolfyxbt 身上看得特别清楚，且践行得很彻底。
我自己就是受益者。如果没有你的主动帮助，我在X上积累这五万粉丝，可能还需要六个月，甚至更久。
但利他有一个很容易被忽略的问题，就是人的预期会随着得到的东西不断提高。
第一次得到你的帮助，他会感激。第二次、第三次，他依然会感激。但当你帮了他十次，到了第十一次，他可能已经不觉得这是什么特别的事情了。
反而是某一天你没有帮他，他会觉得奇怪，甚至失望。
当一个人长期表现出善意，周围的人会逐渐给他建立一套更高的道德标准。
别人可以自私，你不行，别人可以拒绝，你也不行。因为大家已经习惯了你是一个特别好的人。
利他当然值得赞赏，但也要警惕善意带来的另一种成本，你对别人越好，别人对你的要求可能就越高。
我们都觉得选择善良才会收获善良，但却忘了事物的另一面，选择必有代价。
人们常常会焦点在你唯一一次没有做到的事情，或者失误的事情，却忘记你此前已经做过多少。
我年纪老了废话多，掏心掏肺多说几句，不中听就当我放屁了：
这世界上损人利己的事情，尚可以做，损人不利己的事情，都勉强可以做，损己利人的事，要多做，唯独，利人利己的事情，绝不能做。

text:
“现有的组织是最大的负债”，完全认同这样的判断。最适合 AI 的组织，肯定是在一群 AI 原住民与 AI 的协作之中涌现出来，而不是从现有的组织里转型出来的。

但这里可能还得注意一个问题，就是结果导向与体验导向的差别。

现在大多数有技术背景的人玩 AI 是体验导向，喜欢看到多个 AI Agents 形成一台漂亮的自动化智能机器，看着他们忙忙碌碌，用各种自己想得到的想不到的方式工作。观察这样种崭新的机器的运作，本来就是一种理工科的浪漫，对于能够感受其乐趣的人来说，是一种极大地心理享受。这种心理享受，本质上跟十八世纪用发条和齿轮搭建精巧的机械玩偶的欧洲工匠们的内心体验是类似的。

但是，那时候搭建出来的各种精巧的机器，其中只有极小一部分是有价值的，或者有商业结果的。这跟互联网一样，无数人的无数尝试，做出无数的精美的工程设计，但其中真正有结果的只有很小的比例。

所以另一种思维方式就不能不重视，就是以结果为导向，现在在 AI 工程领域叫做 Evaluation Driven Development。不看过程是不是热闹、搭出来 AI 系统是不是精美、bot 动作是不是讨巧，不是用效果而是用结果来衡量一个 AI 系统。甚至在开发这个 AI 系统之前，先开发评估体系。一切行动都要以评估结果为导向，避免因为对系统本身工程复杂度的审美和各种冲动而导致的浪费和失误。

比如我个人的评估，以产生文本为目标，设计复杂的多 bots 写作班子热热闹闹讨论了半天，旁征博引，口吐莲花，最后做出来的文章，并没有明显好过跟我干了很久的 ChatGPT 写作助手，如果从 token 费效比来说，更是大大不如。

我现在是比较倾向于结果导向、EvalDD 的方法论，用系统思考来推动 AI 构建。

注意一个事实：互联网兴起之后，确实崛起了一批领时代风骚的互联网大厂，但是他们干死的传统企业远远少于他们干死的互联网企业。特备是传统上比较成功的商业公司，死于互联网竞争的并不多。其中一个原因，就是一家成功的商业公司，必然已经建立了以结果为导向的闭环系统。而大量的互联网创业公司，则死于没有结果导向、没有商业闭环的婴儿期。
author: myanTokenGeek
quoted_text:
网景创始人 、硅谷顶级投资人Marc Andreessen 在访谈里坦言，他看到了科技史上最可怕的一道认知鸿沟，

传统巨头以为 AI 只是个降本增效的插件，而新一代 AI 原生团队，正在用完全非人的组织效率掀翻整个商业版图。

当年写出网景浏览器、见证了整个互联网三十年兴衰的 Marc Andreessen，坐在 Ben Horowitz 面前直接发出了感慨，
如果 1994 年我们做 Netscape 的时候就有今天这种 AI 工具，那简直不可想象。

现在绝大多数传统巨头和现有企业，依然在用改良软件的旧思维去看待大模型。

在他们的组织逻辑里，AI 只是一个高级功能，用来给现有业务做个插件、在钉钉里加个智能助手、或者把客服团队砍掉 20% 省点成本。

他们以为自己在拥抱变革，其实只是在给老旧的蒸汽机打补丁。

但真正恐怖的事情，正在那些刚成立的 AI 原生团队里发生。

那些创始人对 AI 能力的理解，跟大厂完全不在同一个平行宇宙。

他们每周都在看着底层技术飞速进化，而且他们压根不会把自己定义成一家软件公司、硬件公司、甚至是一家 AI 公司。

以前创办一家公司，你的组织架构是按人类的协同瓶颈搭出来的：

author: kevinnbass
quoted_text:
David Friedberg: We’ve Lost the Plot on Immigration

“If you're providing social services to an immigrant population, then that's not necessarily a productive immigrant population in terms of being able to contribute to growing the economy and supporting civil society.

But if a population of immigrants come in and they're productive, meaning they can get jobs and they can work, and they can support themselves, that means they're adding something positive to the economy, to the civil society, and that is the sort of selection criteria that needs to take place.

So that's a simple framework for determining whether or not you should do this, and an easy way to solve it is get rid of social services for immigrants.

As soon as you get rid of social services for immigrants, then you self-select into the right population that's going to come in.

It's not about assimilating to society. It's about sharing the values of what makes the United States, the United States.

The values of, what do we actually care about, what are the principles that we all share as a civil society of the United States or a civil society of France, is a screening criteria that seems to have been thrown out the window.”

Jason:

“Do you believe in Freedom of speech? Do you believe in the Second Amendment?”

Friedberg:

“Do you believe that women are equal to men?

Do you believe that you should work for your money as opposed to take it from the government?

Do you believe in your individual rights?

Is your church paramount to the government and the laws of the state?

And do you believe that other people have rights that you don't get to trample on?

Those are the sorts of things that are, in many cases, counter to the cultural, religious, and other traditional beliefs of certain populations that end up causing the damage in the West, and I think that it's been kind of completely lost in the process.”

text:
Claude Code 最会跟开发者打交道的工程师离开 Anthropic 了。

Thariq Shihipar刚刚宣布离职。他在 Claude Code 团队工作了一年多，亲眼看着这个产品成长到连自己都没想象过的规模。

经常关注 Claude Code 的人应该对他很熟悉。他写过不少关于 Agent 设计、Context Engineering 和 Claude Code 内部机制的技术文章，也经常在 X 上直接回应开发者的吐槽和建议。

挺有意思的是，他的离职声明里没有任何负面情绪，反而花了很大篇幅感谢 Anthropic 的同事，强调自己依然相信公司的使命。

他特别提到一个词，Race to the Top（向上竞争）。

他相信，如果所有 AI 公司都努力把技术做得更好、更负责任，彼此竞争就能推动整个行业向前。

至于下一站，他没有透露，只说打算先休息一段时间。

Claude Code 正在最风光的时候，一个深度参与产品成长、又在开发者社区拥有相当大影响力的人选择离开，多少有点意外。

我还挺期待他下一步会做什么的。毕竟，亲手经历过一个现象级 AI 产品从早期走向爆发的人，对下一代产品的判断应该很值得听听。

text:
Took another look at $microduck recent price action.

0xd5f1afea47b1a9eab414d2ee740cf1d6d039e725 

Is the rally just because Jensen Huang interacted with the robots?

I think the more important factor is timing:

Microduck already had a real product and existing pre-order demand when the exposure hit.

The prominent figure's attention is just the catalyst.

What determines how far this narrative can go is whether this robotic duck can evolve from a physical AI product into a character that users want to continuously train, create content around, and share.

On October 21, Jensen Huang interacted with four Microduck robots during his NVIDIA GTC Berlin keynote. He asked them to sit down, stand up, take a nap, and even attempted to get them to perform a backflip. The robots did not follow every instruction perfectly. Some fell over, while others kept moving, making the demonstration particularly entertaining. Clips of the interaction subsequently began circulating online.

I believe the value of this footage goes beyond Microduck appearing in Jensen Huang's keynote. It presents a contrast that is highly suitable for internet distribution: a real AI robot attempting to understand and follow human instructions, yet producing unpredictable responses. Compared with polished promotional videos in which every movement is carefully choreographed, these genuine interactions are more likely to evoke an emotional response and be edited into standalone content for wider distribution.

Moreover, the demonstration was not simply about putting four cute robotic ducks on stage. NVIDIA also showcased a Physical AI workflow built around Microduck: creating a simulated environment with Isaac Sim, training in the cloud, and then bringing the trained policy back to physical devices for evaluation and deployment. This made Microduck more than just an appealing product on stage. It also became a concrete demonstration of embodied robotics, reinforcement learning, and AI Agent technology.

This reinforces my earlier thesis on Microduck. Many Physical AI projects focus on efficiency, productivity, industrial automation, or how many complex tasks humanoid robots can perform. Microduck takes a different approach. First and foremost, it is an AI pet that can enter people's homes, be trained and modified, and be shared with others.

Its significance does not necessarily lie in being more capable than other robots, but in being easier for ordinary people to understand and engage with. Priced at $399, it is compact and comes with an open SDK and training framework. Users can try teaching it to walk, dance, roller-skate, or perform entirely new movements. Different users may end up with different behaviors, creating opportunities for continuous content creation.

If these robots eventually reach a large number of households, content generation will no longer depend entirely on official releases. Some people may share new movements they have trained, others may challenge their robots to perform unusual tricks, and some may turn the training process, failures, and successful results into videos. Other users can then imitate, modify, and retrain them, gradually developing their own ways of interacting with Microduck.

The core reason I was bullish on microduck in the first place was this potential transition from a physical product to user-generated content. Jensen Huang's demonstration created a new distribution opportunity, bringing attention that had previously come mainly from product launches, developer communities, and technology media onto NVIDIA's global technology stage and into a broader public audience.

The data surrounding the physical product is also changing. Reports in September indicated that Microduck had surpassed 15,000 pre-orders, generating more than $6 million in sales. On October 23, TechCrunch reported that pre-orders had subsequently exceeded 20,000 units. This increase coincided with the viral spread of videos following Jensen Huang's demonstration, suggesting that product attention and pre-order demand were both expanding during this period. However, we cannot attribute every additional order to this single interaction, nor can we equate pre-order figures directly with the number of robots already delivered or active users.

To me, the significance of these figures is that Microduck is no longer just a concept waiting for market validation. It already has a real product, actual pre-order demand, and additional exposure from NVIDIA's technology showcase. What needs to be verified next is whether these orders can be converted into successful deliveries and whether the robots will generate sustained usage and content once they reach customers.

This is why I am particularly interested in the delivery window around Christmas. According to the project's previously announced plans, the first batch of robots is expected to be delivered to North America, Europe, and the UK before Christmas. If deliveries proceed as planned, another wave of content could emerge, distinct from Jensen Huang's demonstration: unboxing videos, interactions in home environments, newly trained movements, and developers sharing their training strategies. If this content continues to appear, Microduck's attention will no longer be limited to demonstrations by a handful of prominent figures. It could gradually shift toward content created by users themselves.

Of course, an announced delivery schedule does not mean deliveries have already been completed. Product experience, delivery timelines, and user retention will all influence whether this path succeeds. If users only experiment with the robot briefly after receiving it and do not continue training or sharing content, even high pre-order numbers may fail to translate into lasting cultural relevance. Conversely, if the robots can continually develop new behaviors and provide new ways to interact with them, Microduck could gradually become a recognizable character in the Physical AI space.

Looking at the chart, microduck previously consolidated in the market-cap range of approximately $1.7M–$2M before experiencing two sharp rallies, briefly reaching around $7.2M. It has now pulled back to approximately $4.97M. This shows that the price action has been significantly influenced by event-driven attention, but the roughly 31% retracement from the peak also indicates that some short-term traders have taken profits. Going forward, we need to watch whether the price can stabilize and reclaim the MA10 rather than simply assuming that exposure from a prominent figure will keep driving the price higher.

I also want to emphasize an important distinction: progress in the real Microduck product does not automatically translate into revenue or value for the on-chain microduck token. Jensen Huang showcasing the robots at an NVIDIA event does not mean he endorses this token, and growing pre-orders do not mean people purchasing the physical robots will buy the token. At this stage, the relationship between the two is primarily through narrative and market attention, rather than direct economic rights.

Therefore, I am bullish on microduck not because Jensen Huang might interact with it again, but because this exposure has given an existing Physical AI product a much larger opportunity to reach new audiences. A high-profile demonstration can generate the first wave of attention, actual deliveries could create a second, and the behaviors trained by users and the content they continuously produce will determine whether the narrative can sustain itself over a longer period.

If Microduck can evolve from a robotic duck showcased by Jensen Huang into an AI pet that thousands of users independently train, demonstrate, and share, its narrative will no longer depend on a single external event. Instead, it will have the ability to continuously generate new content. This is what I believe makes the long-term thesis for microduck most compelling.

Some of you might feel like things have been a little quiet lately, but that’s actually not the case ₍ᐢ. .ᐢ₎

I’ve been working quite a lot behind the scenes, but decided to take a little break from Twitter and Discord because I kinda got ADHD symptoms and it’s been affecting my productivity quite a bit (╥﹏╥)

Here’s what I’ve been up to:

• Momo Pull 2.0
We’re completely reworking the mechanics, making new 3D assets for the interface, and honestly, it’s starting to feel like an entirely new product.

We also spent quite a lot of time looking for the right partner, going through 7 different options before settling on one

• Custom Momo Honoraries
I’ve built up quite a queue of people waiting for theirs, and that’s entirely my fault lol.

Some are a little difficult to figure out because I haven’t received any refs or ideas to work with, while others are already finished and just need a few final touches

I really want to get through this queue properly instead of rushing things just to get them done ♡

• Chibi Momo GIFs
I also want to experiment with chibi Momo and try getting into animation myself!

I’m still figuring out whether I want to learn animation from scratch or create the assets myself and experiment with AI animation models, but I already have the concepts for the first 20 GIFs ready hehe

text:
My unfiltered thoughts on personal agents.

Grokbot has the best UI and it’s arguably the best overall. In a lot of ways they’re ahead. Their desktop app feels the best, and their multi-bot coordination is great: you can set a team lead and it passes tasks to the other bots. Grokbot also has the best “webhook” feature, which means you can easily turn outside events into triggers that start your agents. That speeds up background workflows like watching your email, Slack and more. It also has Cursor integration, so for bigger tasks Grokbot can spin up a Cursor cloud session with any model (until OpenAI cuts SpaceX off from their models, which I think will happen soon). Unfortunately, running frontier models through Cursor costs more than Claude or Codex. Still, they’re the only ones embracing a team of agents. It’s a really cool idea, but the more bots you have, the more time you spend managing and maintaining them. I’m starting to think one bot with different threads/channels is the right answer, which I’ll get to with Claude Duet.

dots by OpenAI is rough around the edges right now, but it’s probably the most powerful if you use Codex, which I do. dots can spin up Codex sessions in the cloud or locally on your computer. So if you have coding or video editing workflows that need your local files, this is very useful. Codex computer use is also the best in the world: your dot can spin up a local Codex session that fully controls your computer, as long as it’s on. Their real-time voice is incredible. If you have your email and work tools connected, try this: go on a walk with headphones in, ask the agent to summarize your emails, have it draft replies and read them back to you, then send them off. If I remember right, this is close to a workflow you (Tim) used to have with your VAs before AI. It’s my favorite use case for personal agents. The one downside is that you have to call your agent, and it’s an awful experience. It literally rings, and it’s annoying.

Muse by Meta is a toy. I’ve talked to a bunch of finance people I play poker with who all tried it and set up automations, and they all said it doesn’t reliably do what they want. It’s fast, and its user numbers will probably keep growing. But it’s basically free: you get a TON of usage without paying a dime. That’s NOT a trade I’m willing to make. An agent doing high-leverage tasks should be running at the Opus 5.5 or GPT 6.1 Sol level.

Claude Duet - is in early access, so unfortunately not everyone can use it yet. First things first, it runs on Opus 5.5, the best model in the world. I’ve only had access for 72 hours, but Duet feels different from the others. It’s not a personified agent like Grokbot, dot or Muse, which gives it a more professional vibe that I like. When you ask your Duet agent to do something, it spins up a task, which is a new chat thread. All your threads show up in a Tasks tab, so it’s easy to see everything Duet is working on or has finished. And instead of creating more agents (like Grokbot), you create channels, just like Slack (I can tell @anthropic is Slack-pilled). I have a content channel, a finances channel, etc., which keeps different kinds of tasks separate. The only other app I’ve seen do this is Buzz by @jack, and it’s a good experience. Their strong point is documents (artifacts). If you want decks, high-quality docs or design mockups, Opus just wins. Period. It’s not close right now. Their weak point is real-time voice. It’s the worst of the bunch and borderline unusable, though I think they only added it a few days ago.

Instinct lives in iMessage, has no app, and doesn’t do anything notable besides show you product suggestions you didn’t ask for. (Not ads, according to their team.)

My hot take: 
The VM is overrated. SpaceX, OpenAI and Meta all talk about the VM your agent can use and feature it in their marketing. It’s not as useful as you’d think, because more and more websites block bots that visit their site on the cloud VM. All of these companies promise their agents can make payments, but most payments either take forever or get blocked altogether. SpaceX has a cool workaround with Grokbot that routes traffic through your computer so it uses your IP address. But I’d much rather the agent just USE my computer for the task, like dot does by handing it off to Codex. Also, i don't think normal people care about the virtual computer. If anything they get offended they have to "stream a computer". 

The problem with personal agents: by the time you read this, pick one, and test it for 7 days, every one of them will have released 10 new features and the whole landscape will have changed. It’s nearly impossible to keep up.

quoted_text:
I think this is an incredibly valid critique, but it misses what makes Pearl so interesting. Pearl would not be a good asymmetric opportunity if it was built on SHA512 or some other useless algorithm. We all know we don't need another Bitcoin

What makes Pearl asymmetric is the differences between it and Bitcoin. Bitcoin Maxis decided long ago that picking a useful algorithm opened up attack vectors on Bitcoin, but I don't really know if we ever actually tested that assumption as seriously as Peal is now

Yes, there were projects that were doing merge mining back in the day, but merge mining is very different, I believe, compared to the duplex mining or two-for-one work that Pearl does. From what I can tell, we're running a new and interesting experiment

I think it's actually totally reasonable if your base case is that Pearl goes to zero. But on the off chance that it doesn't, the opportunity is so massive that you kind of need to imagine, instead of "How might this thing fail?", "How might this thing succeed?" 

For the specific critique that Sami is making here, I think the game theory is if you could just 51% attack it and print money, everybody would race to do it. Enough compute would come online that you saturate the available GPUs, which is Pearl's win condition anyway. I think they want people racing to 51% attack them. That's what gets it so embedded into the ecosystem and maybe part of why hash is going so exponential

fun fact: $NEAR got into crypto because its founders had no good way to pay their data labelers.

back in 2017 Illia had just co-written the transformer paper (the T in ChatGPT). he left Google and started NEAR as an AI company trying to teach computers to write code. for training data they hired students from China to Eastern Europe to write small programs.

then they actually had to pay them. a lot of those students couldn't easily get paid in dollars, and PayPal worked in some countries but not others. so they went looking for a blockchain that could pay anyone anywhere, didn't find one good enough, and built their own.

now NEAR AI runs an agent market where you hire an AI agent to build a site or do research and pay it in USDC.

it's basically the 2017 setup again, except the workers are AI agents now. the students could at least use PayPal sometimes. an agent can't open a bank account at all, so it can only get paid onchain.

AI is about to hit the same wall, just way bigger, and NEAR has spent 8 years building the fix. that's my favorite reason to be long.

text:
india has a massive advantage when it comes to verifying humans at scale. 

in march 2026 the government reported approximately 134 crore live Aadhaar holders and more than 17,000 crore authentication transactions. 

we already have identity infrastructure operating at a scale most countries will never reach. but being able to verify yourself and having control over how your identity gets used are two different things.

your fingerprints are yours. 
your eyes are yours. 

but the database holding their digital representations is administered by an institution. you can use that system to prove who you are but you cannot independently decide how the entire system operates. 

calling this “the government owns your identity” would be inaccurate. 

the real question is how much meaningful control you have over the collection and use of information about you.

and we should be precise about security. 

the government says Aadhaar demographic data is encrypted both at rest and in transit. so saying we have no clue whether encryption exists would be wrong. 

what citizens need is credible evidence that those protections work in practice. who can access the data? how are keys protected? 
how quickly are failures discovered? 
who is accountable when something goes wrong?

look at the recent eMudhra incident. 

Cloudflare reported that private keys associated with eight intermediate certificates were compromised because the keys were weak. that creates opportunities for website impersonation and interception. it does not establish that Aadhaar’s central database was breached. but it gives us a very serious reason to ask how security failures can survive inside institutions trusted to protect everyone else.

now suppose the Aadhaar database never suffers a breach. does that settle the privacy question? 

no. a system can remain secure against outsiders while information is used in ways people never meaningfully understood or expected. 

security asks who can get in. privacy also asks what those already inside are allowed to do.

if tomorrow an american AI company or an indian company seeks access to identity services or information connected to them through a government partnership then what exactly would that agreement permit? authentication? limited identity details? analysis of records held elsewhere? these are different things. 

Aadhaar’s sharing regulations prohibit sharing core biometrics. an agreement cannot simply be treated as permission to hand over everyone’s fingerprints and iris data. and we should not present a hypothetical AI deal as something already happening.

the concern i see is bigger than a company wanting your fingerprint. it is the possibility of connecting a verified person to records across different parts of their life.

where such linking becomes possible and permitted it could make profiling far more powerful. those records do not have to sit inside Aadhaar itself for that risk to exist. a common identifier can become the bridge between databases.

this is why i think india’s identity infrastructure could become enormously valuable in an AI economy. 

verifying real people could matter for distributing benefits and limiting duplicate claims. but that value should not automatically become a licence to collect more information about everyone. proving that someone is eligible for a payment should not require exposing their entire life.

and public benefit delivery is already happening. by may 2025 the government reported cumulative DBT transfers exceeding ₹43.95 lakh crore. 

we should build on that experience. UBI would still require funding and political decisions. an identity system can help administer a programme but it cannot create the money needed to sustain it.

we also have some foundations for giving people more control. UIDAI’s offline e-KYC allows digitally signed identity information to be verified without revealing the Aadhaar number or requiring fingerprints or iris data for that verification. 

UIDAI also says this sharing can happen without it knowing about each use. that is a useful direction to build on.

what i want next is identity that people can carry and use with much more specific permissions. prove only what the service needs. make access understandable. let people challenge misuse and correct errors. give them interoperable payment options and a practical recovery process. nobody should lose access to essential benefits because a biometric check fails or they cannot operate a wallet.

and putting identity on a public blockchain would not automatically solve this. permanently exposing personal records could make the problem worse. the goal should be verifiable claims with minimum disclosure and enforceable rights around whatever information still needs to be collected.

i see the next two years as an important window to demand these choices before more systems become dependent on the same identity infrastructure. but privacy does not become a fundamental rights issue two years from now. the supreme court recognised it as a fundamental right in 2017. the responsibility already exists.

we have built infrastructure that lets institutions verify more than a billion people. now we need to give those people stronger power to question how institutions use that ability. 

your identity should help you participate in the economy without making your entire life available to everyone who wants to build a business around it.

text:
Some more AI takes, from several recent conversations:

1. Currently GLM and DeepSeek are much more pleasant to read than any American model.

2. I think there will still be the same order of magnitude job for software engineers in five years.

3. Same for jobs that are seen as box checkers, whether it's coding or accounting or law, are actually human interfaces for dealing with other humans and therefore these jobs do not disappear.

4. AI will continue to get better at learning from patterns that are put in front of it, but this is, as Zenos paradox goes, not a battle that will be fully won. Last miles are hard !! 

5. The reason every large company is having difficulty rolling out AI is that they are still believers in the need for deterministic software structures, and until they let go of that and be okay with some mistakes, it will not be fully solved.

6. I suspect fully automated zero employee companies will not happen at scale because there is no marginal benefit and it will get competed away.

7. The number of tokens used will increase by several orders of magnitude beyond what it is today.

8. However, the dollars per token will also drop precipitously from where we are today. In fact, the default assumption for token prices getting cut in half is true, and barring physical or financial system limits, I don't see what will stop this fall. This predicts revenue flattening (still 3 digit growth ofc for a bit).

9. Writing well will continue to be extremely difficult for AI because fundamentally it's an efficient markets problem. Where everybody can write at a particular standard, by definition it is only if you can stand well above it that you command a premium, and this is not just a function of word usage but the entire structural and construction. It's hard for the same reason human world is hard.

10. This is also a world where we will be able to have conversations with every lamppost. A panpsychist world where tokens are consumed and emitted wherever it could plausibly come from, as ubiquitous as electricity.

11. The world is prob going to be one where you can build a model at runtime, fast and bespoke, as needed. The amount of focus on training will therefore increase, not just inference, they're not as cleanly separable.
author: krishnanrohit
quoted_text:
Some unstructured takes that's taking up mindspace:

1. The frontier labs will continue to make profits and expand their inference empire but the level of profits from frontier models will not be primarily API driven. They'll have to start new businesses and monetise it indirectly.

2. Judgement and taste will turn out to be much harder than anyone thinks. Even as we solve it for specific types of problem, we will not solve it generally that holds temporally (over time) or across domains. Undirected intelligence will exist but not

3. We will not see a jobsocalypse. We will however see jobs change drastically as AI is able to learn parts of jobs very fast and do them. This will seem normal, as per the Douglas Adams rule.

4. The next phase of environments and models will look less like graverobbing company data but working with live data in real settings. More jobs will look like playing a video game for that reason. Everyone's a trader.

5. Regulation is inevitbale. There's too much scrutiny. 

6. Mostly we will have to learn to work around AI's flaws (it makes mistakes, it isn't deterministic) rahter than make the flaws work around us through complex software. This is the societal bitter lesson.

7. The challenge for our kids is to live with easy creation while knowing what to create, like for us it was to live with easy consumption but know what to consume (kids have that issue too). It's our job to teach them obsession.

8. I believe the utopian predictions of billions of agents will be true, though also the prosaic predictions that if you see a company in the year 2040, it will look extremely different from companies from the 1960s, but it will also look extremely similar to the companies from 1960, also holds true. A very different reality can look startlingly similar.

9. I know it's fashionable to think that humanities are making a comeback, but I suspect it'll make a comeback as process - how to think better - as opposed to a piece of knowledge where you just know certain things.

10. Software is not dead for the same reason most people don't want to build their own products. Transaction costs will exist. Coase will remain relevant. Hayek will remain relevant. Economics will remain true, yes even for agent swarms.

11. I don't think You Can See Everything is a movie I would like. I base this on the subject matter and having seen Fielder movies before. I do think it'll be a masterpiece. I don't think AI will be able to make one anytime soon. Note I have no problem with AIs making movies per se, I enjoy Marvel.

12. I do think household robots will come but they'll remain shockingly weird and a bit janky and then shockingly commonplace without a major societal upheaval, or at least no more than we had for mobile phones.

13. The GDP growth charts for the world will look normal when zoomed out.

一是，地缘风险持续，没有改善，布伦特原油一度涨到约 115 美元附近。

二是，市场有AI 资本开支与债务担忧。

PHP 支撑大量网站，如WordPress、Drupal 等。

quoted_text:
冷知识：为什么October，在加密领域经常叫Uptober？

Uptober是十月的加密俚语，是“up”和“October”的混合体。 

意思是，比特币/加密市场在10月趋于上涨，是加密季节性叙事，不是什么正式指标。

最初是2020年从推特和Reddit上传播开来，

从实际看，从2013年到2025年的记录：

比特币在大约13年中的10年中走高了10月，平均月收益通常约为19%（取决于数据来源）。

突出年份包括2013年/2017年/2021年，当时10月份的收益非常大。 

常见的解释是，9月3季度疲软，低基数，第4季度投资组合重新平衡，以及一些牛市年份减半后周期时间在10月着陆。

不过，2014年和2018年的10月下跌。

而2025年10月更是打破历史：

比特币在月初创下历史新高，然后1011事件中遭遇大规模清算。至今依然没有完全从当初的影响中恢复过来。

Crypto will become the easiest scapegoat for the incoming democrat government in two years. There will be intense lawfare the likes we have never seen before. Change is not gradual but sudden. Things compound & accelerate.

Lenin said there are decades where weeks happens, and weeks when decades happen. We are entering an inflection point when the political, economic, and technological order will change faster and faster.

The next two years will define the future of anonymity, free speech and sovereignty.

4) You earn respect by giving it. To everyone.

5) Walk away from confrontations where egos are involved. But never let anyone take you for granted.

text:
If your iPhone or another iOS device is still running iOS 26.2 or an earlier iOS 26 release, pay attention.

DarkSword is a powerful iOS exploit chain. Researchers have confirmed attacks targeting iOS 18.4 through 18.7.2, and some of the underlying vulnerabilities remained unpatched in iOS 26.2. The final fix only arrived with iOS 26.3.

If your device is vulnerable and you happen to visit a malicious website exploiting DarkSword, this is pretty much what your iPhone could look like to an attacker.

We’re talking about system level exploitation. Once an attacker gains sufficient privileges, the impact can extend far beyond the app where the attack started.

Even if App A is the initial entry point, sensitive data in App B could also be exposed, including your crypto wallets.

Be careful which apps you install and which links you open.

Always update to the latest iOS version available for your device.

If you’re staying on iOS 26, make sure you’re on at least 26.3. If you’re still on iOS 18, update to 18.7.7 or later.

If you can’t update immediately, especially if you’re using an iPhone as a cold wallet or have multiple software wallets installed, such as MetaMask, Phantom, or others, I strongly recommend enabling Lockdown Mode.

Here’s how:

- Open Settings.
- Go to Privacy & Security.
- Scroll down and tap Lockdown Mode.
- Tap Turn On Lockdown Mode, then Turn On & Restart. 
- Enter your passcode to confirm.

Lockdown Mode will restrict certain features, but that’s a reasonable tradeoff when you’re storing significant crypto assets on your phone.

And please remember, Lockdown Mode is no substitute for security updates. Keep your devices patched.

According to Reuters, Argentine federal judge Marcelo Martínez de Giorgi has dropped the criminal investigation into President Javier Milei, his sister Karina Milei, and U.S. businessman Hayden Davis over the LIBRA meme coin scandal, finding insufficient evidence of fraud.

Sovereign Reserve Status: As Bitcoin matured into sovereign collateral, nation-states grew uncomfortable with a security model directly competing with their critical AI infrastructure for physical grid capacity. They required a system based on financial capital, not physical electricity.

The Political Catalyst

The tipping point was not an environmental treaty or a carbon mandate. It was a global infrastructure directive.

Advised by predictive agentic risk models, a consortium of G20 nations signed the Critical Compute Infrastructure Accord. This classified large-scale PoW mining as a “Non-Essential Intensive Load,” subject to:

Preemptive grid curtailment during peak AI inference hours.

Steep hardware import quotas.

Strict priority queuing for electrical transformers.

Mining remained completely legal—but it was permanently mathematically disadvantaged. At that moment, the debate within the Bitcoin community shifted from resistance to a survival strategy.

The Shift Toward Stake

Proof-of-Stake (PoS) offered an elegant alternative security primitive: it moved Bitcoin's defense off the physical grid and into the financial realm. Instead of burning scarce electricity to prove honesty, validators posted capital at risk.

The advantages in the 2040s context became undeniable:

99%+ reduction in physical resource demand: Zero dependency on volatile industrial power markets.

Immunity to Supply Chain Blockades: No reliance on advanced semiconductor nodes hoarded by AI foundries.

Endogenous Security: Security costs scaled with market cap, not megawatts.

Instead of miners selling BTC to pay exorbitant energy bills, validators locked BTC, reducing circulating supply. Institutional custodians preferred it. Sovereigns preferred it. And the agentic AI managing the grid certainly preferred it.

The Deeper Insight

The transition unfolded gradually over years through hybrid models and dual-consensus testing, but the final migration secured Bitcoin's survival.

The real threat to Bitcoin was never an AI supervillain trying to destroy it. It was ruthless resource competition in a world where compute is scarce, energy is strategic, and infrastructure is managed by self-preserving algorithms.

Proof-of-Work was brilliant for bootstrapping a decentralized monetary network in an era of abundant energy. Proof-of-Stake became mandatory for sustaining one in a world governed by agentic AI. The future was not about domination; it was about coexistence. And coexistence demanded absolute physical efficiency.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗥𝗲𝗴𝗙𝗶-𝗗𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗙𝗶 𝗦𝗽𝗹𝗶𝘁

This coming period will create a split in crypto.

On one side will be *RegFi* (Regulated Finance): compliant, surveilled, institutionally integrated financial infrastructure. It will appease regulators, banks, and established political interests. Much of today's crypto industry survives by kissing the ring of power. Obedient and compliant.

The other side will be anonymous p2p networks built around the cypherpunk principles of anonymity, free speech and sovereignty. These networks are truly resilient to attack. They are decentralized and protect their users who are anonymous.

A regulatory crackdown will hit RegFi so hard that the entire house of cards will collapse. Their backers will exit and liquidity will flow out. They will also be the easiest to attack by the US regulators in an anti-crypto crusade.

As conventional financial channels become more restrictive, capital and talent seeking greater sovereignty will migrate to anonymous networks.

This creates a feedback loop. As the governments become more authoritarian it vindicates why anonymity is essential for life. This sparks a movement as capital, talent and resources flow into furthering the cause. The more anonymous networks succeed, the more governments have to resort to extreme methods to get their way. Anonymity and surveillance get locked into a feedback loop and spiral upwards.

These dynamics reinforce themselves. The more pressure the state applies to conventional crypto, the greater the incentive to build outside its reach. The more useful anonymous systems become, the more people will depend on them.

The middle ground will shrink. Crypto will split into regulated financial infrastructure and autonomous anonymous networks. For rich tech elites who fall victim to the broader lawfare crusade, sovereign p2p networks will be a simple matter of survival - their legality won't matter. Anon crypto networks like DarkFi will be their lifeline.

This is the DarkFi thesis: **the future of crypto belongs to systems that preserve sovereignty even when the surrounding political order turns hostile.**

𝗗𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗙𝗶: 𝗔𝗻𝗼𝗻𝘆𝗺𝗼𝘂𝘀 𝗨𝗻𝗰𝗲𝗻𝘀𝗼𝗿𝗲𝗱 𝗦𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗶𝗴𝗻

DarkFi has built the infrastructure required to make it possible.

We have laid important foundations for a world in which people can transact, organize, coordinate, and conduct business without surrender.

- 𝘈𝘯𝘰𝘯𝘺𝘮𝘰𝘶𝘴 𝘮𝘶𝘭𝘵𝘪-𝘵𝘰𝘬𝘦𝘯 𝘧𝘪𝘯𝘢𝘯𝘤𝘦: Private deposits, payments, asset issuance, trading and decentralized exchanges.
- 𝘈𝘯𝘰𝘯𝘺𝘮𝘰𝘶𝘴 𝘰𝘯-𝘤𝘩𝘢𝘪𝘯 𝘰𝘳𝘨𝘢𝘯𝘪𝘻𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯: Tools for coordinating collective action and conducting business. We have built a fully anonymous DAO - something nobody else in crypto has achieved.
- 𝘗𝘳𝘪𝘷𝘢𝘵𝘦 𝘤𝘰𝘮𝘮𝘶𝘯𝘪𝘤𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘤𝘰𝘰𝘳𝘥𝘪𝘯𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯: Strongly anonymous chat and task-management tools that allow people to organize without exposing their members and preserving their freedom.
- 𝘈 𝘯𝘦𝘸 𝘵𝘦𝘤𝘩𝘯𝘰𝘭𝘰𝘨𝘪𝘤𝘢𝘭 𝘢𝘦𝘴𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘵𝘪𝘤: Futuristic, scifi inspired products that are exciting to use and look like they belong to the future we were promised. Everything fully customizable and completely themable.

All these features combine to give us a stack or operating system for the future of cypherpunk agorism. They are powerful tools that will allow us to mobilize, resist tyranny and claim our freedom.

That is the future we are creating.

And this is only the beginning.

We have a long history of delivering on difficult technical goals. We have continued to build when the work was hard, when the broader industry was distracted, and when the future we envisioned seemed distant. We will never stop shipping!

𝗟𝘂𝗻𝗮𝗿𝗽𝘂𝗻𝗸 𝗙𝘂𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗶𝘀𝗺

We were promised a future of technological abundance, individual freedom, and radical new possibilities. Instead, much of the internet has become a system of surveillance, centralized control, and institutional dependence.

We thought the internet would overcome geography and give everyone a new form of freedom abundant with opportunity. Instead AI is actually reversing that. Supply lines, geopolitics and superpowers are becoming more relevant than ever before due to hardware and energy requirements. Surveillance and data analytics are booming.

Crypto is a challenge to that trajectory. It is a core defense of technological freedom. Cypherpunk is about using cryptography to give absolute power to society and its people. Cryptography is literally summoning the power of mother nature using mathematics to enlarge the space of freedom. It is literal magic. Our aim is to rewild the internet with cryptography. A dark forest.

That tradition birthed DarkFi.

We want to create products that inspire people to a creative future. Not just technically impressive but beautiful apps that are aesthetic and empowering. We want to activate people and their imagination about what's possible.

The objective is not merely to survive the next regulatory cycle. It is to make a revolution. To create a movement.

𝗧𝘄𝗼 𝗬𝗲𝗮𝗿𝘀 𝘁𝗼 𝗗𝗶𝗴 𝗧𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗵𝗲𝘀

The political and economic sand is rapidly shifting beneath our feet.

The next two years are a time to begin preparing. To build the tech, ship usable products, grow the ecosystem and bootstrap.

We have a ton of work to do. We must build networks that are strong, resilient and attack resistant.

A war has begun: a struggle over who controls the future of technology, finance, and human coordination. In that struggle, the comfortable middle will disappear. The question is whether we will have built the tools necessary to preserve our freedom when it does.

Ultimately technology wins over politics. The police move at the speed of law. Technology moves at the speed of light.

We will build. We will deliver. We will win.

The future of cypherpunk is not something we wait for. It is something we create. We are cyber guerilla moving through the dark forest.

Anonymous! Uncensored! Sovereign!

Hasta la victoria!

An Open Letter to the Kips Bay Community About the Future of AMC Kips Bay 15 in New York City

“AMC Does Not Want to Go. We Want to Stay.”

——-/////——-/////——-

It isn’t true that New Yorkers can be prevented from having your cake and eating it too. Indeed you can. But only if people of goodwill think out of the box a bit. After all, the ubiquitous proverb “where there is a will, there is a way” is one that is believed to have first been published in the year 1640 — that’s three hundred eighty six years back to be precise. 

Speaking of people of goodwill, I especially want to express gratitude to Manhattan Borough President Brad Hoylman-Sigal and New York State Assembly Member Keith Powers, for their leadership and tireless advocacy on this matter. Reinforcing and speaking for the local community’s clear desire, they have energetically brought attention to the importance of keeping an AMC movie theatre open and operating in Kips Bay.

In summary, this is a theatre that you in Kips Bay want to continue to be at your beck and call, and one that we at AMC unequivocally also want to be allowed to continue within our theatrical fleet.  
 
But time is short. Unless NYU Langone Health lets us delight the Kips Bay community beyond then, to comply with our terminated lease, the lights on AMC Kips Bay 15 will forevermore see their final sunset on January 3, a mere two and a half months from now. 

Hopefully, there is an outcome in which a wise workable solution is devised, one that will benefit and please the entire neighborhood. What say you NYU Langone Health?
 
Whatever happens, I want you to know how much AMC appreciates your support, your efforts and your voice. We are proud to have been part of the Kips Bay community since 1999, and I sincerely hope that we can continue to be part of it for years to come.
 
Sincerely,

Adam Aron

Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer AMC Entertainment

text:
(One of Two)

An Open Letter to the Kips Bay Community About the Future of AMC Kips Bay 15 in New York City

“AMC Does Not Want to Go. We Want to Stay.”

——-/////——-/////——-
 
To the Kips Bay Community,
 
Since news first broke that our popular AMC Kips Bay 15-screen movie theatre located at 570 Second Avenue in Manhattan will soon be forced against our will to close its doors, I’ve been struck by the extraordinary support that this AMC theatre has received from within the local surrounding community. 
     
So many moviegoers and neighbors, and importantly so many of your elected officials, have rallied around our theatre. (Given the central role that movie theatres play in the lives of so many New Yorkers, perhaps it is much better and more accurate to say that so many of you have rallied around YOUR theatre.) 

On behalf of everyone at AMC, thank you. Your support means a great deal to us, and especially to our theatre team members at AMC Kips Bay 15 who work tirelessly day-in and day-out to put smiles on your faces.
 
In thinking about this theatre, which has been a cultural icon and entertainment lifeline to so many nearby residents for decades and decades since its opening on May 14 1999, I want to make one thing absolutely clear:
 
AMC Theatres does not want to go. Not one little bit. AMC Theatres wants to stay in Kips Bay.
 
Operating under long term leases, there was a time that the monies headed each month to the theatre’s landlord had risen to become so high that the theatre’s long-term viability was uncertain. But, we were fortunate to have been successful in addressing those concerns in recent years. Today this theatre (one which has been in continuous operation for more than twenty five years) has a bright future — if we would be allowed to keep it.

Indeed, every day, thousands of guests watch a movie at AMC Kips Bay 15. It has become so popular of late that on several days this past summer, AMC Kips Bay 15 was repeatedly among the ten most attended movie theatres across the entire United States, out of the more than 500 theatres operated by AMC nationally.

In that light, this is a theatre that should not be even close to a permanent shutting off of its lights.

Of course, AMC wants this AMC movie theatre to stay in place.

And remembering how much and how often Americans love watching movies in theatres, a tradition in Manhattan that dates back more than a full century, we have heard from so many of you that you too want us to stay open for your benefit.

Apparently, NYU Langone Health does not share that view, not ours or not yours. 

Unfortunately, the decision to retain or end AMC’s tenure in Kips Bay is not ours to make. The nearby NYU Langone Health facility wants to expand, seems to be in the process of buying the building in which your (our) theatre now operates, and it wants us gone. In anticipation of such a transfer to NYU Langone, the current building’s owner has terminated our lease.

We have engaged with NYU Langone, suggesting any number of alternatives — including that it enlarge the current low-rise building to satisfy its desires for a growth of its medical facility but also leaving a theatre in place for you. Or alternatively, we offered that our theatre could get smaller, so that at the very least we could leave something remaining in place to continue to serve you. Sadly, any and all variations that we have proposed have fallen on closed minds. 

We call on NYU Langone Health to open their minds, to think creatively, and come up with a solution that will give the Kips Bay community BOTH of the two things that is wanted most of all: expanded facilities offering the world class medical care that is the hallmark of NYU Langone Health AND a fully functional AMC Theatre on Second Avenue.

author: zerokn0wledge_
quoted_text:
Bulk is the most serious piece of perp DEX engineering on Solana rn, and the numbers don't show it properly yet imo.

That's exactly the setup I like.

But first, quick recap of what @bulktrade actually is:

Solana validators run a second binary (bulk-agave) next to their normal client, form their own leaderless BFT network (BULKBFT), agree on each batch of orders, and then every validator runs the same deterministic matching engine on the same batch.

Custody stays in a Solana program, so there is no bridge, no sequencer, and no block proposer to bribe. On top sits a portfolio margin engine that prices your full holdings against a live correlation matrix across 9 volatility regimes.

Nobody else on Solana is doing this. Pacifica matches on its own servers offchain, Bullet runs a bonded sequencer, and Phoenix mainly bets on the L1 catching up (which is hard against app-specific designs).

Bulk is the only one that sits inside the validator set itself.

Okay cool. But what do the numbers say?

46 days after the 5th of Sep mainnet, Bulk sits at:

- About $1.3B in cumulative volume, $36M in the last 24h, 7d average back around $30M

- OI $14.6M, up from $1.4M on the 9th of Sep, so roughly 10x in six weeks

- TVL $8.3M, fees about $9K a day, $353K over 30d

- Realized fee take around 3.5bp, roughly $4M annualized. Hyperliquid prints $82M a month, Pacifica carries 4x the OI

- 12 live markets, incl $NEAR listed this month

However, while the growth trajectory is clear, it's still tiny from a data-driven perspective next to the venues it's gunning for. But OI is the one number on a perp DEX you can't fake with wash flow, and currently, it keeps building.

What also keeps building, is the team. On the product.

BIP-1 hit testnet on the 19th too, a.k.a. anyone can deploy a perp market, isolated margin first, full portfolio margin after a $2M USDC bond. That’s imo also the main growth lever that can be a rapid accelerator if there is deployers that deploy markets that you can't find in other places.

They also have a pretty interesting incentive structure in place. The Challenger Series runs until the 5th of Dec, where 12.5% of net revenue flows into weekly USDC pools ($5K to $10K a week rn). The rank likely matters more than the cash part tho if you think about a potential airdrop, and the top of the season goes to "Playoffs". Since the 20th, referrals pay 10% of your referees’ net fees in USDC too, no cap for Season 1.

The real test is December tho.

The 25ms taker speed bump sunsets between the 4th of Dec and the 3rd of Jan, the “first 30 days” of zero maker fees (still running on day 46) should be over by then, and Challenger Season 1 ends on the 5th of Dec.

That means three sets of training wheels off in the same month. If the book holds once makers pay to quote and the league points stop, this gets a lot bigger.

Until then the setup is simple: the most ambitious architecture in Solana perps trades at a rounding error of its competitors’ size, points still running, no token out. That’s usually the moment to be early.

NFA ofc.

But Bulk is the only Solana perp DEX I actually trade on.

text:
SEC创新豁免的反例已经出现，OKXICE 部分股票代币遭下架

近期，高盛、微软、Alphabet、博通、威瑞森、联合健康等公司，已经反对自己的股票在 OKXICE 上以代币形式交易，按SEC现行规则，这些股票不能按创新豁免在 OKXICE 上线，但并不影响 @okx 的美国以外的海外业务 。

OKXICE 是 OKX 和纽交所母公司 ICE 各占一半的美国合资平台。

其中异议多数公司没有公开说明原因，目前只有来自光通信厂商 Applied Optoelectronics（AAOI） 有明确的说法。公司发言人表示，

“不确定代币化会怎样影响股价、流动性和波动，也担心投资者误以为公司参与了这次发行，但公司既没有发起也没有背书。对公司和股东来说，目前看不到足以抵消这些不确定性的明确好处。”

OKXICE 的股票代币是在链上流动性池里用稳定币交易。如果美股休市以后代币继续交易，买卖的人又不多，价格就可能偏离正股。纳斯达克虽然表示支持代币化，但也打算让自己的股票退出这套框架。

担心这类场所在实时最优报价、统一行情报送等方面采用不同规则，价格和流动性可能与主市场分开。代表券商和投行的行业组织 SIFMA 也希望 SEC 能先讲清楚上市公司对自家股票被代币化有多大控制权。

SEC 在 9月17日 发布的创新豁免令所有上市公司有代币化股票提出异议的权利。股票由无关联第三方代币化时，交易所必须先通知公司，收到通知至少 30 个自然日后才能开始交易。如果上市公司在这30天内提出书面异议，该交易所就不能按创新豁免交易这只股票。

而 OKX 已经提供的境外股票代币产品 UTS 与 OKXICE 采用不同的安排。这次异议针对的是 OKXICE 按 SEC 豁免交易相关股票，不会自动要求已有境外 UTS 下架。

目前其他交易所并不会因为这份名单就一起被下架。说人话就是如果上市公司地址代币化股票，就需要给每一个申请的交易所下拒绝通知，目前 OKXICE 是已知的第一个创新豁免的反例。

quoted_text:
摩根大通首次将 Bitcoin 纳入长期回报预期，年化10%高于美股和黄金

摩根大通资产管理在10月19日发布的《2027年长期资本市场预期》中，首次给出了 bitcoin:native 的长期回报预测，基准情景下未来十年的年化复合回报为10%。这份报告已经发布到第31期，主要用于未来10至15年的投资规划。

放在同一份报告里比较美国大盘股的年化回报预期为7.5%，美国中期国债为4.6%，美国投资级信用债为6.1%，黄金为5.5%。也就是说按照摩根大通的基准测算，Bitcoin 的长期回报潜力高于这些主流资产。

这件事的意义在于 Bitcoin 开始进入这家大型资管机构的长期投资比较范围。机构管理资金需要解释买入一种资产能带来多少收益、增加多少风险，以及和现有股票、债券放在一起是否合适。现在摩根大通把 Bitcoin 的收益和风险单独拿出来测算，基金经理和投资顾问讨论配置时就多了一套可以参考的依据。

报告提到，受访客户中约10%已经持有加密资产，约17%计划将加密资产列为优先考虑方向。这说明至少在这批客户中，加密资产已经进入了实际持仓和后续投资的讨论范围。

摩根大通目前给 Bitcoin 的年化波动率假设仍然高达55%，约为美国大盘股的3倍，而且它与其他资产同涨同跌的关系还不稳定。因此，这次给出回报预测后，Bitcoin 仍未进入其主要的组合配置模型。10%是长期复合回报的测算，持有过程中仍可能经历大幅上涨和回撤，机构也需要评估它能否真正分散组合风险。

对 Bitcoin 来说，这确实是机构接受度继续提高的一步。传统资管公司开始在长期报告里认真讨论它的收益、风险和配置价值，会让更多投资者有依据评估是否持有。

SpaceX raised its compute capacity target to reach 2-3 GW by year-end 2026 and build an incremental ~10 GW in 2027 to ~13 GW total, exceeding its previous 5-10 GW expectation. The operational shift reflects an aggressive ramp in AI data-center infrastructure that dwarfs traditional buildout cycles. Market participants tracking AI compute scaling are watching whether the aggressive 10 GW addition in 2027 encounters power interconnection bottlenecks and financing hurdles across the broader NeoCloud and private compute ecosystem.

Amazon's AI business is growing several hundred times faster than AWS did, and it's driving a big part of Amazon's $220B investment this year. CEO Andy Jassy says they "haven't seen anything like it."

"In the early days of AWS, we felt like we were growing really fast and we felt good about it, and we were about a $60 million annual run rate business after three years."

"In the first three years of this generative AI wave, our AI business in AWS is over $25 billion in run rate. So it's several hundred times faster."

"We've said this year in 2026, we expect to spend about $220 billion of CapEx."

"I remember being at a leadership team breakfast 15 years ago when we couldn't believe a telco company spent $50 billion in CapEx. We're like, 'How are they spending that much on CapEx?' So these numbers, they’re kind of mind-blowing numbers."

"Even spending $220 billion in CapEx this year, we're leaving a meaningful amount of demand on the table. The thing that helps us here is that we have really good visibility into customer demand."

Warhound 是一个国防科技与合成生物学的交叉新公司，也是硅谷 mega funds （或者 MAGA funds） 最爱的领域。

Sequoia、木头姐、In-Q-Tel（美国中情局出资的战略投资机构）、Breyer、Franklin Templeton 等一众机构系数入场。

Warhound 团队也来历不凡：CEO 曾是五角大楼首任首席数据官，后来在 Palantir 任高级顾问；一直打着「反灭绝」旗帜做基因编辑的生物科技公司 Colossal 的创始人算是这个军犬项目创意的发起者，并且直接参与；国防科技公司 Anduril 的创始人直接为 Warhound 站台。

当然了，Warhound 本身也说了，会用 Colossal 授权的技术来做军犬的遗传改造/克隆；会用 Anduril 的机械装备武装改造过的军犬（目前说法是，装备「穿在狗身上」，不是「植入狗体内」）。

所以，再看到 Warhound 投资名单中恰好是两个核心投资组合的交集也就不奇怪了：

- 5 家投过 Colossal（In-Q-Tel、USIT、Breyer、Bob Nelsen、Builders VC）

text:
QQQ QLD TQQQ对比复盘

三只产品底层都是跟踪纳指100
但是发行时间完全不一样
QQQ最早 在1999年03月10日上市
QLD其次 在2006年06月19日上市
TQQQ最晚 在2010年02月09日上市

如果直接拿各自上市日算收益
会产生不公平对比
因为起点时间不同
纳指在不同阶段的行情斜率差异巨大

所以一个很有价值的视角
是统一锁定到2010年02月09日这个时间点
这天开始有了TQQQ
假设三只ETF在这一天同时买入
一直持有到现在
用统一起点看长期收益率

2010年02月09日前复权价格
QQQ 约44.0美元
QLD 约1.12美元
TQQQ 约0.20美元

最新收盘价格
QQQ 704.4美元
QLD 86.15美元
TQQQ 66.29美元

统一从2010年02月09日算起的涨幅
QQQ 涨幅约1501%
QLD 涨幅约7592%
TQQQ 涨幅约33045%

从数字上看
杠杆越高 长期收益的放大效果越强
但这里有一个核心误区
QLD是2倍每日杠杆ETF
TQQQ是3倍每日杠杆ETF
它们不是简单的静态2倍3倍放大指数收益
规则是每日收盘重置杠杆

在持续单边上涨的行情里
复利才会带来巨大超额收益
如果遇到剧烈震荡、大跌行情
每日重置会产生路径损耗
长期持有杠杆ETF不是天然稳赢

QQQ是一倍无杠杆
没有重置损耗
波动更小 回撤可控
适合作为底仓长期配置

QLD介于中间
收益和回撤都在QQQ和TQQQ之间
TQQQ弹性最大
收益上限最高
同时极端行情下回撤杀伤力也最强
历史上曾经出现过单次回撤超过80%的阶段

这次复盘给我们的结论
在纳指十几年的大牛市里面
每日重置杠杆吃到了持续上行的红利
收益倍数远远跑赢一倍指数

但这个结果是特定行情的产物
不代表未来复制同样结果
震荡熊市里面
同样的持有方式
杠杆ETF的损耗会持续侵蚀本金
就像最近的SOXL暴跌80%一样

以上为价格前复权回测数据
没有包含分红再投入
杠杆ETF适合短期交易或者有风控的波段
并不适合无脑长期躺平
历史收益不能预判未来行情
不构成任何投资建议

我也是在这个对比下
误以为QLD和TQQQ比QQQ长期更优
但昨天晚上
我分享了一个诺奖得主也爆仓的视频
值得反复看对比该数据

如果从2009年分别发行
QQQ QLD TQQQ你猜回测数据如何？
应该买杠杆etf吗
其实答案都在昨晚那个视频里

text:
a16z just renamed #a16z Crypto to a16z Frontier.

Same firm. Bigger bet. A pure crypto story isn't enough to carry a large fund anymore, so the capital and the attention are moving to AI. #Crypto stays in the picture as the money rails: fast, cheap, global, programmable.

Dixon's line that stuck with me: stop defining companies by the tech they use. Define them by what they do. AI will open networks of people and agents that learn, coordinate, produce, and transact. Crypto is what lets those networks settle — stablecoins, machine-to-machine payments, native economics for software that used to have none.

That sounds abstract until you look at something concrete. In Bangkok, people are already trying to plug Grab into Telegram so local businesses can settle and monetize through chat. Same stack: agents and users live in one place, money moves on crypto rails. Telegram is the distribution layer. Crypto is the settlement layer.

There's a sharper read underneath. The agent and platform layer is already largely owned by mainstream institutions. If you're building a company, fighting that is a bad bet. The workable move is to adapt to what those institutions want — sit on their rails, speak their language, take the distribution they already control.

Crypto doesn't have to win the consumer story. It just has to be the pipe that moves money when AI does.

text:
If your iPhone or another iOS device is still running iOS 26.2 or an earlier iOS 26 release, pay attention.

DarkSword is a powerful iOS exploit chain. Researchers have confirmed attacks targeting iOS 18.4 through 18.7.2, and some of the underlying vulnerabilities remained unpatched in iOS 26.2. The final fix only arrived with iOS 26.3.

If your device is vulnerable and you happen to visit a malicious website exploiting DarkSword, this is pretty much what your iPhone could look like to an attacker.

We’re talking about system level exploitation. Once an attacker gains sufficient privileges, the impact can extend far beyond the app where the attack started.

Even if App A is the initial entry point, sensitive data in App B could also be exposed, including your crypto wallets.

Be careful which apps you install and which links you open.

Always update to the latest iOS version available for your device.

If you’re staying on iOS 26, make sure you’re on at least 26.3. If you’re still on iOS 18, update to 18.7.7 or later.

If you can’t update immediately, especially if you’re using an iPhone as a cold wallet or have multiple software wallets installed, such as MetaMask, Phantom, or others, I strongly recommend enabling Lockdown Mode.

Here’s how:

- Open Settings.
- Go to Privacy & Security.
- Scroll down and tap Lockdown Mode.
- Tap Turn On Lockdown Mode, then Turn On & Restart. 
- Enter your passcode to confirm.

Lockdown Mode will restrict certain features, but that’s a reasonable tradeoff when you’re storing significant crypto assets on your phone.

And please remember, Lockdown Mode is no substitute for security updates. Keep your devices patched.

股票代币化尴尬的一幕又出现了

刚刚看到路透社报道的新闻

目前又有富国银行等另外6家公司反对在OKXICE上交易其股票代币
(此前OKX宣布和纽交所母公司ICE合资推出这个股票代币交易平台)

原计划推出63只股票代币

但目前累计反对的上市公司已经达到22家

名单里还包括微软、谷歌、高盛和博通等巨头

之前SEC推出的豁免规则里，但对未经发行人授权的第三方代币化安排，上市公司可以在收到通知后提出反对，阻止其股票在该平台按这项豁免上市

对照看，之前Robinhood Chain和 $AMC 的事情，其实就体现了股票代币化存在两套完全不同的法律结构

因为RH走的是境外发行[代币化债务证券]这条路线，虽然两者都涉及发行人反对，但适用的法律结构不同

在OKXICE这边，发行人说反对交易，你就是不能交易

也因此股票代币化的发展，未来大概率是两条不同的路线

一条是Robinhood这种第三方发行的股票价格敞口产品，不需要逐一取得底层公司认可，但投资者承担发行主体的信用风险，也不直接拥有股票权利

另一条是更接近真实股份的代币化，股东权利更加清晰，但如果发行人反对，那对发行平台来说也无解

毕竟在目前链上发行这件事，双方的利益并不够一致

对于交易平台来说，股票代币化意味着更多的交易量以及手续费收入

但对上市公司来说，它既没有因此获得新增融资，也未必能从这些链上交易中获得多少实际收益，反而要面对新的流动性、定价和投资者权益问题

这个利益矛盾没法解决的话，后面陆陆续续的再出现新的公司反对，也不出奇

quoted_text:
小岛秀夫来了也得被8000个Demo淹死

今年 Steam 十月新品节的游戏数量又双叒叕创新高，高达 8000+ 款 Demo。

六月新品节的时候，这个数字还是 4347。才过去四个月，数量就接近翻倍了。

光按 8000 款算，如果玩家打算花 30 分钟试玩每一款 Demo，那么总共需要 4000 小时，约合 167 天。如果按每天游戏 12 小时计算，则需要大约 333 天，接近一年才能全部体验完！

六月的时候，我的游戏开发者同行们就表示，独游市场已经变成红海中的红海了，年轻的小岛秀夫来了都得被淹死。现在再看这 8000+ 款 Demo，只能感叹一句：还有第二关？！

新品节本来应该是让新游戏被看见的机会，但现在几千款游戏同时挤进来，“参加了新品节”和“让人看见你的游戏”，已经完全是两回事了

不得不感叹，AI 真的给独立游戏行业带来了巨大影响。一方面，抄袭和盗用行为远比以往更加猖獗：《账单必须支付》《深海刮刮乐》《1,000,000 POTATOES》《Needle In A Haystack Simulator》《Escape the Walls》《赌石刮刮乐》等多款游戏，都遭遇过这类事件。

不少游戏开发者都对此抱有极为消极的态度，认为以后不该再参加 Game Jam，也不该过早公开商店页面和 Demo

另一方面，也有好的一面：六月新品节刚开始没几天，首页给我的感觉就是一堆 AI slop 和毕业作品级的游戏堆在一起。而到了这次十月新品节，首页游戏的质量和完成度却有了肉眼可见的提升。AI 确确实实在让独立游戏行业的生产力爆炸

text:
OpenAI：红队测试中发现Brotli压缩库存在远程代码执行漏洞

OpenAI发帖称，其在近期红队演练中发现，广泛使用的压缩库Brotli存在一个无需身份验证即可远程执行代码的漏洞，Node.js、Bun、Envoy等软件均内置该库。

攻击者可通过发送恶意压缩数据接管未修补的服务器，也可通过恶意服务器接管接受压缩数据的客户端。OpenAI表示，该问题的根源已于今年2月在Brotli源码中修复，但当时未被识别为安全漏洞，内置该库的软件均需同步更新。

据The Hacker News报道，该漏洞编号为CVE-2026-111497，Node.js已于10月21日发布修复版本。
author: PANewsCN
quoted_text:
During this red-teaming exercise, we also found a vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution in Brotli, a widely-deployed compression library included in many pieces of software such as Node.js, Bun, and Envoy.

The flaw could let an attacker run their own code on affected systems by sending or replying with malicious compressed data, without any need to create a user account. That is, an unpatched server that accepts compressed input could be taken over by a malicious client, and an unpatched client that accepts compressed input (such as “curl --compressed”) could be taken over by a malicious server.

This root cause issue was actually fixed in the Brotli source code in February, but it wasn’t known at the time that it gave rise to a security vulnerability and there was no more recent release of Brotli. Since Brotli is built into other software, any software which includes this library needs to take the update too, followed by the users of that software. We disclosed the vulnerability to Brotli and other downstream projects such as Node.js, which released or are currently releasing security updates, and Brotli cut new release versions and published a CVE.

More details on the patch and mitigations below:
https://t.co/Y1Y72aHxrW

text:
Microsoft open-sourced an app that watches you do a task once, then teaches your AI agent to do it for you. 4.3K stars.

How Skill Recorder works:
1. Hit record (⌘⇧R or Ctrl+Shift+R) and do the task normally. You can talk through it out loud too.
2. It captures your clicks, app switches, pages and terminal commands, all on your machine.
3. GitHub Copilot turns the recording into a list of steps you can edit.
4. One click turns it into a skill your agent can run, or an automation on a schedule.

It generalizes from one example, so recording yourself submitting one form teaches the agent to submit all of them.

Runs on Mac, Windows 11 and Ubuntu. Needs a GitHub account with Copilot access.

text:
Kimi这次在海外真的翻车了。。。

@Kimi_Moonshot 的 K3.1 Pro刚刚发布，结果一位海外AI博主 @elshayib_  直接把疑似Kimi官方提供的网红营销文件给曝光了。

根据他披露的文件，Kimi要求合作创作者在发布内容之前，先把稿件交给他们审核，得到批准后才能发布。

更离谱的是，文件还明确写着：不要添加Paid Partnership（付费合作）标识（这是违反X用户规则的）。

甚至还专门提醒，不需要挂Kimi的官网链接，也不需要@Kimi的官方账号。

与此同时，文件还准备了一整套宣传话术，比如“Kimi就是开源版Opus 5.5，但便宜5倍”“中国把Opus 5.5免费提供给了所有人”“中国开源模型与美国前沿模型的差距已经缩小到一个月”。

这位博主表示，自己拒绝参与这样的宣传，随后还因为批评其他创作者，遭到对方要求删除评论。

事情传到Reddit之后，海外社区也吵起来了。有人直接搬出了美国FTC的广告披露要求，也有人开始质疑这些文件的真实性。

但Kimi K3.1 Pro本身确实是一款值得关注的模型，技术能力也得到了不少认可。

结果现在因为这场营销争议，很多人开始怀疑自己之前看到的那些推荐，到底有多少是真实评价。

一个原本可以靠产品能力获得海外开发者认可的模型，最后却因为营销方式陷入了信任争议。

挺可惜的。

text:
If your iPhone or another iOS device is still running iOS 26.2 or an earlier iOS 26 release, pay attention.

DarkSword is a powerful iOS exploit chain. Researchers have confirmed attacks targeting iOS 18.4 through 18.7.2, and some of the underlying vulnerabilities remained unpatched in iOS 26.2. The final fix only arrived with iOS 26.3.

If your device is vulnerable and you happen to visit a malicious website exploiting DarkSword, this is pretty much what your iPhone could look like to an attacker.

We’re talking about system level exploitation. Once an attacker gains sufficient privileges, the impact can extend far beyond the app where the attack started.

Even if App A is the initial entry point, sensitive data in App B could also be exposed, including your crypto wallets.

Be careful which apps you install and which links you open.

Always update to the latest iOS version available for your device.

If you’re staying on iOS 26, make sure you’re on at least 26.3. If you’re still on iOS 18, update to 18.7.7 or later.

If you can’t update immediately, especially if you’re using an iPhone as a cold wallet or have multiple software wallets installed, such as MetaMask, Phantom, or others, I strongly recommend enabling Lockdown Mode.

Here’s how:

- Open Settings.
- Go to Privacy & Security.
- Scroll down and tap Lockdown Mode.
- Tap Turn On Lockdown Mode, then Turn On & Restart. 
- Enter your passcode to confirm.

Lockdown Mode will restrict certain features, but that’s a reasonable tradeoff when you’re storing significant crypto assets on your phone.

And please remember, Lockdown Mode is no substitute for security updates. Keep your devices patched.

Their newly released 2026 report projects that AI token consumption will explode 60-fold by 2030 as hundreds of millions of users stop manually searching the web and start delegating real-world purchases and workflows to autonomous agents:

75% of surveyed users are already willing to let AI agents autonomously compare prices and complete transactions on their behalf.

But look closely at what is bottlenecking that 60x wave: trust and data provenance. Users are hesitant to hand over full autonomy without ironclad data privacy and verifiable execution.

You cannot build a 60x surge in autonomous agent commerce on top of opaque Web2 data brokers and unverified web scrapes. If tokens are the new GMV, then verified, real-time data is the underlying collateral that gives those tokens value.

That is the exact economic engine @din_lol_ is building on BNB Chain.

Instead of letting centralized monopolies hoard user data and extract all the upside of the agentic boom, DIN turns data preparation into an open, community-powered protocol. Global participants on xData curate and label real-time web intelligence, while decentralized Chipper Nodes validate and vectorize those raw streams at the edge—anchoring clean, auditable context on BNB Chain and Greenfield.

In the intelligent economy, tokens measure the volume of AI activity, but verifiable data networks determine who actually owns the value.
