text:
Was about to write this but Ben beat me to it. Econ is unique among the sciences in that it is several pretty different fields living under one umbrella. 

Empirical econ is the biggest subfield and its closest to biology or chemistry: it’s about designing or—even better—finding a natural experiment, or documenting interesting and important patterns in data. Most of the arguments in that field are about methods, eg do you have identification. More and more are starting to study AI now but obviously this won’t be transformative AI because, well, there is no data on transformative AI. 

Then there are macro economists. They work with a set of pretty standard models and mainly expand them by slowly adding/subtracting different sectors or micro founding factors of production in different ways. Many of the arguments are on the parameter values that we should assume when simulating the economy. Early research on transformative AI started there—as demonstrated recently by Chad, Anton et al, the different levels of transformation are due to different assumptions on parameters rather than some new type of economics. The same model can predict basically no impact of AI vs huge transformation, it’s all about assumptions on parameters. 

Finally there is micro theory. This is where decision theory, game theory, mech design, org econ (sort of) live. This field works by setting out a set of assumptions and then *deriving* the expected results; alternatively one could start with a result and work backwards to derive the necessary and sufficient assumptions. There is a ton of potential here to do work on transformative AI: start with assumptions on how AI differs than human agents (eg relax basic assumptions on constraints, on scarcity, introduce completely different objective functions), then derive implications. But this is where there is the least amount of work, and it’s important for that to change (and I believe that it already is). 

I think we can make a ton of progress from these three subfields on better understanding the potential AGI and post AGI transformation. 

But there is another scenario, post strong ASI, where I don’t think economics has much to say about. Here I agree with @Jabaluck that the economy (if you can even call it that) and the agents in it will be so vastly different and beyond our imagination that I wouldn’t know where to start modeling it. Not to discourage others, but post singularity seems like pure epistemic uncertainty to me. 

A lot of the critiques I hear about AI and economics come from people who don’t quite get what economists do. They look around at different results and if they don’t like some of them, they say “oh economics isn’t “pilled” or something. But economists don’t debate results, they *derive* results from assumptions. Thats where the debate is. Saying “but you don’t understand a world with 15 billion  AI agents”. What does that mean for the economy? What are those agents doing, who is buying what they are producing, what do property rights look like? Depending on those assumptions you’ll get vastly different economic scenarios, from 2% growth and high human labor share to completely alien centralized systems with no prices or markets.

text:
My post about Hitler and the far right got millions of views. Clearly, it hit a nerve. So today I'm going to show you, step by step, why the notion of "far right" as it's used in France makes almost no sense. And why the people who wield it are usually the last ones who should be lecturing anyone.

Let's start with the only question that matters: what makes a political system work or fail? To a very large extent, it's the economy. A country that produces wealth, that lets its citizens create, trade and build, stays standing. A country that destroys that collapses, no matter how beautiful its slogans are.

And in economics, there are really only two worldviews.

The first is collectivism. The idea that the State knows better than you. That it must plan production, set prices, run companies, decide what you earn, what you buy, and eventually what you think. The individual is just a cog serving a grand collective project: the class, the nation, the race, the people.

The second is freedom. Capitalism, property, individual liberty, individual responsibility. The idea that millions of people creating value for one another produce infinitely more prosperity than an office of planners, however brilliant they may be.

Now look at the list of the great totalitarian regimes of the 20th century. Stalin: total planning, forced collectivization, millions dead. Mao: the Great Leap Forward and the deadliest famine in human history. Pol Pot: money abolished, cities emptied, nearly a quarter of Cambodia's population exterminated. Mussolini, the man who coined the word fascism: "Everything within the State, nothing outside the State, nothing against the State." And Hitler, leader of the National Socialist German Workers' Party, whose program proclaimed "the common good before individual good." He subjected the entire German economy to State plans: the Four-Year Plan, frozen prices and wages, unions dissolved into a single state labor front, industrialists producing whatever the regime decided.

Their flags were different. Their designated enemies were different. But the machinery was the same: the individual doesn't exist, only the collective matters, and the State decides everything.

Why does it always end in totalitarianism? Because collectivism doesn't work. And when a system doesn't work, it has only two options: admit failure or force people. They always choose force.

Ludwig von Mises proved it as early as 1920: without free prices, without a market, a planner simply cannot know what to produce, how much, or at what cost. He is flying blind. A planned economy isn't a less efficient version of the market. It's an impossibility.

Friedrich Hayek drew the political conclusion in 1944 in The Road to Serfdom, a book he dedicated "to the socialists of all parties." One chapter is titled "The Socialist Roots of Naziism." Another, "Why the Worst Get on Top." For Hayek, controlling the economy isn't controlling one sector among others. It is "the control of the means for all our ends." Whoever controls your bread controls your life. Then your speech. Then your thoughts.

Milton Friedman put it his own way: a society that puts equality before freedom ends up with neither.

So we know exactly what works. It's not an opinion. It's a century of real-world experiments. Listen to the Austrian school, Mises and Hayek, with Friedman from Chicago alongside them: economic freedom, limited government, individual responsibility.

And this is where we get to the great accusatory inversion. Part of the left-wing press spends its time screaming fascism. Why? Because the fascism fantasy is the best way to never talk about the track record of their own ideas. Deep down, they know: if their collectivist program were applied all the way, it wouldn't work, because a collective economy cannot work. And an economy that doesn't work always ends up having to coerce, surveil and ban. In other words, it becomes exactly what they claim to be fighting. The real heirs of totalitarian logic are not the ones being pointed at.

So who gets called "far right" in 2026? People who want safe cities. People who want to keep their culture. People who just want to live a peaceful life, raise their kids, and not have to board up their shop every weekend. People who want the law to apply to everyone.

If that's the far right, then the word no longer means anything. And maybe that was the point.

Polymarket significantly changed the rules for the second time yesterday on the Russia x NATO military clash market, after $7m had already been traded.

The new rules state that interceptions of strikes on ships in NATO countries territorial waters (which is sovereign territory), won’t be considered as a military clash.

The original rules did not have any such carveout and it is impossible to know where Polymarkets bar-raising will finish before we place a bet on these markets. For example, would an intentional drone strike on Bucharest that is intercepted count if the target was a foreign-owned civilian building? Would the US defending a cruise ship from a drone strike while it’s docked in Miami count? (Weirdly, a recon drone shot down over any of those targets would 100% count)

Although I don’t agree with it, I don’t have a huge problem with the actual ruling of the specific incident that was clarified yesterday. I believe the pattern of strikes on nearby ships, alongside statements from President Dan and EU officials, provided strong enough evidence of targeting Romanian territory. But it's a judgment call that could go either way.

The trouble is the bar has now been raised significantly again for future incidents when millions has already been traded, and we can’t accurately price these markets without predictability that rules won’t change under our feet.

text:
The market still prices $NEAR like an L1 that missed its moment. It's 74% below its 2022 high

@Bitwise prices it as the chain AI agents run on, with a $155 base case for 2030. That's about 30x from $5.26

BlackRock's research paper "The Machine-Native Economy" describes the same outlook. Agents that find, buy, and pay for compute on their own

In the paper's words, agents "query real-time marketplace APIs to compare available capacity by price, performance, latency, location, and hardware specialization," then pay "on a per-use, per-model-token, or per-job basis"

NEAR already runs two pieces of that:

1. NEAR Intents: you say what you want and solvers route it across chains. $33.99B in volume to date, $4.84B in the last 30 days (DefiLlama), and its fee share has bought back NEAR since February
2. NEAR AI Cloud: private inference inside secure hardware, now a provider on OpenRouter, and running private sessions in Brave's Leo assistant

When I asked Matt Hougan on @MilkRoadDaily whether Bitwise's call was absurd, he said NEAR could 40x or 50x, and that "doesn't strike me as absurd if it actually executes on this vision"

His framing: Intents alone roughly justifies today's price, and the AI goal comes "like a moonshot for free"

For context, $155 a NEAR works out to about a $200B market cap. That's still below ETH's $298B today

Wall Street is already buying in. Bitwise's spot NEAR ETF launched Sept 29 and took in $35.5M on day one, which Hougan called "a Bitcoin ETF style success"

It's important to say that these price predictions are ambitious, and not necessarily going to play out in NEAR's favor. Ryan Rasmussen said their model assumes "a very high likelihood that this doesn't work out," and the bear case in the report is $1.63

If agents end up buying their own compute, the chain built around that job looks cheap at a $6B market cap

It's a risky bet, but the upside is a huge moonshot.

Full disclosure: $NEAR is a position in my Milk Road PRO portfolio. Our PRO team was early to $UNI (+54.8%), $AERO (+93.7%), and $SOL (+39.1%)

text:
US stock valuations are facing a notable divergence, with September 2026 data showing the S&P 500 trading at a 5-year CAPE of approximately 28.3x, while 10-year real yields are about 62 basis points higher than potential real GDP growth.

-> Real interest rates are putting pressure on valuation ratios, but the stock market is maintaining high P/E ratios, near the levels seen during the peak valuation periods of 2000 and 2021.

Historically, valuation ratios are often high when real yields are slightly lower than potential real growth.

When real yields fall too far below growth, inflation can erode valuation ratios; conversely, when real yields significantly exceed growth, high capital costs often put pressure on P/E ratios to narrow.

The current position is on the side of higher real yields over growth, but CAPE remains near 30x – a mismatch between discounted conditions and market valuations.

Corporate earnings, growth expectations, and the concentration of high-quality businesses could sustain high valuations for longer than anticipated. However, with high CAPE, the market will be more sensitive to changes in real yields and earnings prospects.

text:
GitHub 上有一个恐怖的开源项目，叫 yt-dlp。它没有华丽的界面，没有庞大的人工智能模型，却拿到了近乎整个视频互联网的钥匙。 

YouTube、B 站、TikTok，全球大量视频网站都在它的支持范围内。只需要输入一个链接，它就能自动提取视频、音频、字幕，甚至批量处理整个播放列表。

几小时的视频，一行命令就能开始下载。 但真正令人震撼的，是这个项目和人工智能结合之后会发生什么。

把 yt-dlp 接上 Whisper，再接上 GPT 或 Claude，一套自动化流水线就诞生了。它可以持续收集公开的视频，转录讲话，提取观点，分析信息，自动生成文章。

以前你需要花三个小时看完一场技术发布会，现在人工智能可以在获取内容后迅速提炼出几十条有价值的信息。

这意味着什么？意味着视频正在从只能由人类观看的内容，变成机器能够大规模处理的数据。过去互联网竞争的是谁能吸引更多人的注意力，未来竞争的可能是谁能让人工智能获取、理解更多信息。

更可怕的是，这个项目完全开源，普通人也能使用。一个免费工具，正在成为人工智能理解视频互联网的重要入口。

Moderna与默沙东合作开发的Intismeran，也叫V940／mRNA-4157，会根据每位患者肿瘤的独特突变，定制一份mRNA“识别说明书”，帮助免疫系统发现并攻击癌细胞。

每份药物最多编码34种患者特异性新抗原。

本次研究用于黑色素瘤患者完成手术之后，目标是降低残留癌细胞导致的复发和转移。它与K药配合：疫苗帮助免疫系统识别目标，K药解除限制免疫细胞活动的抑制信号。

🟠 Ⅲ期结果：在现有标准治疗上，增加了多少效果？

INTerpath-001纳入1,137名肿瘤已完整切除、仍有较高复发风险的IIB—IV期患者。

757人接受“疫苗＋K药”，380人接受“安慰剂＋K药”。疫苗最多注射9剂，K药治疗约一年，中位随访24.6个月。

最重要的两个结果：

• 复发或死亡风险降低42%，HR＝0.58。
• 远处转移或死亡风险降低38%，HR＝0.62。

两项结果均达到统计学显著性。

两年无复发生存率为82.2%，对照组70.0%，提高12.2个百分点。对照组本身已经使用有效的K药，因此，这是在现有治疗基础上取得的额外获益。

🟠 会场这页历史对照，说明了突破的难度

此前，在黑色素瘤术后辅助治疗中，多次尝试给PD-1药物再搭配一种免疫药，都未能显著改善无复发生存：

• CheckMate 915：搭配CTLA-4抗体，HR＝0.92。
• RELATIVITY-098：搭配LAG-3抗体，HR＝1.01。
• KEYVIBE-010：搭配TIGIT抗体，HR＝1.25。

这些联合尝试还增加了副作用。

这次个体化疫苗做到HR＝0.58，证明这条技术路线能够在一个此前多次尝试失败的场景里，继续增加疗效。

🟠 哪些患者获益？能否证明活得更久？

不同病期、不同年龄的大多数分组，结果方向支持联合治疗；部分小样本分组仍有较大不确定性。

更关键的是，总体生存数据尚未成熟。

会议报道披露，总体生存HR＝0.77，目前未达到统计学显著性。能否显著延长患者生命，仍需继续随访。

现阶段已经证明减少复发、减少远处转移的获益。82.2%的两年无复发生存率，也不能直接当作治愈率。

🟠 副作用是否明显增加？

3—5级治疗相关不良反应：
• 联合组14.2%，对照组13.4%。

全部原因的3级以上不良反应：
• 联合组23.6%，对照组20.3%。

这两个口径要分别看。

联合组常见反应包括发热52.2%、注射部位疼痛51.0%、疲劳38.5%。公司表示未发现新的安全信号。

据会议报道，治疗相关不良反应导致停用任一研究药物的比例为14.0%，对照组8.7%；联合组有2例治疗相关死亡，均被归因于K药，没有死亡被归因于Intismeran。

🟠 一人定制一份药，生产能否跟上？

Moderna官方确认：进入联合治疗组的患者，疫苗生产成功率超过99%。

会议报道还披露：
• 共筛查1,749人，其中302人因肿瘤样本不足被排除，占17.3%。
• 91%的随机入组患者识别出了可用于设计的34种新抗原。
• 首次接受疫苗的中位时间为64天。

🟠 到底符合预期吗？

市场会前没有统一标准。

公开报道中：
• William Blair把HR不高于0.70视为积极结果。
• UBS曾以0.65作为参考。
• Leerink认为低于0.60会是令人振奋的结果。

实际无复发生存HR＝0.58，达到了这些门槛。

但部分资金期待更接近0.50的强劲效果。RBC提到，一些投资者期待0.50—0.59，0.58落在这一范围获益较弱的一端。

评价是：临床结果扎实，达到了多家机构公开提出的标准；相对更乐观的股价预期，惊喜程度有限。

此前Ⅱ期随访得到的49%与本次Ⅲ期42%，来自不同人群、样本量和随访时间，不能直接得出“疗效退步7个百分点”的结论。

🟠 数据有效，为什么股价还跌？

核心数据10月22日因提前泄露而公开，MRNA当天收跌17.6%。

此前股价已经大幅上涨，部分资金期待的内容还包括：更强的疗效，以及这项技术未来能在多个癌种取得成功。

这次黑色素瘤Ⅲ期，验证了一个重要适应症；肺癌、肾癌、膀胱癌等领域，还需要各自的临床数据。

🟠 对未来股价，如何看待

短期，这份结果降低了黑色素瘤项目的研发风险，对基本面有利；股价仍可能大幅波动。

中期，重点看审批和商业化。公司提到2027年潜在获批，但具体时间仍待监管决定。

另外，按合作协议，Moderna与默沙东的成本和利润原则上各分一半，估值时需要考虑这一点。

长期，更大的上行空间取决于其他癌种能否复制效果。目前INTerpath项目包含9项Ⅱ期、Ⅲ期试验，其中3项正在开展的Ⅲ期针对非小细胞肺癌。

结果评价：黑色素瘤Ⅲ期已经交出一份有分量的答卷。下一阶段，审批进展、真实销售，以及其他癌种的独立验证，会逐步决定它能支撑多大的长期价值。

quoted_text:
About the intismeran presentation at #ESMO26 $MRNA $MRK 

My impression of discussant talk given by Inge Marie Svane of the University of Copenhagen was that she was positive if not overly enthusiastic about INTerpath-001. 

"Measured" might be the best, single adjective. 

"Brutal" is how an investor in the audience described the tone of her talk to me. (He was short Moderna, so there's that.) I disagree.  Brutal is too harsh. If people were expecting Svane to jump for joy, then yes, she did not meet that expectation. To me, she played it mostly straight down the middle. 

She took no position on the mRNA vaccine vs neoadjuvant debate. (Slide below)

She noted the lack of intismerna OS benefit, but said the same about neoadjuvant therapy. She also noted greater toxicity associated with neoadjuvant. 

For intismeran, Svane also raised the question about what exactly was driving the vaccine’s benefit — was it the specific targeting of the neoantigens, or was it the general immune boost that studies have suggested mRNA vaccines generally provide?

Again, we're truly sorry to everyone affected.

text:
Ken Griffin, who runs Citadel, just admitted that the biggest advantage of giant funds, armies of people and billion-dollar budgets, is disappearing

And for the first time in history, a small team with AI can move faster than a hedge fund

He’s seen it in his own firm. His AI agent does in 2-3 hours what used to take Citadel’s PhD researchers 6-8 weeks

A fund runs one cycle: come up with a strategy, turn it into code, test it on history, deploy it to the market

Every step used to cost separate people and years of training. Now AI does the whole cycle

You describe an idea in words, it writes the strategy itself, runs it on years of real data, and if it’s alive, deploys it straight to a broker

But the speed isn’t the point. The point is what the retail trader doesn’t understand

You take a strategy with a beautiful chart and you believe it. But a beautiful chart is no proof

Run enough versions and a profitable curve will appear even on random numbers. One just got lucky, and you decided you found gold

Funds don’t trust any curve until they test it on data the strategy has never seen. There the fit falls apart, and a real edge survives

I ran two of the most-cited quant papers through this cycle

Time Series Momentum on Bitcoin: +1,537%. Alive

Betting Against Beta, a classic from every textbook: minus 7.78% a year while the market rose 14.86%. A corpse

One still prints money, the other died long ago. And trading blind, you’d never know which is which until it took your deposit

Griffin says the future belongs to small teams with AI. But the only ones who win are the ones who test before they bet

How to plug your AI into real market data so it runs this exact test instead of guessing, in the article below

体脂率、肌肉量、尤其骨密度的临床标准（图4）。
是高端家用8电极体脂秤、Inbody也无法代替的。

今年1月我发了下方引用推，关于
“骨骼健康重要，但被普遍低估的底层逻辑”。
当时做了一次DEXA检测，
对下肢的骨密度不太满意。

后来因为卧推受伤，
所以我3月开始打网球，至今半年，周均3小时，
减少约2/3的上肢无氧训练。

昨天10月4日我再检测，骨骼改善效果相当明显：
髋部股骨骨密度 +6.4% （图1）；
年龄增加，但全身骨密度不仅没流失，还小幅增加；
内脏脂肪 398g➡️355g，-10.8%

相当于这半年，我用自己身体实验，
完全验证了⬇️引用推里，
关于优化骨骼方法的第5~7层理论。

下半身的骨骼质量
≈
下半生的腿脚好不好，还能不能活蹦乱跳

这么长期一举多得的事情，得保持做。
接下来要再接再厉，把网球常年打下去，

We owe you an apology.

On October 20, we detected unauthorized access to our official website. After verifying API activity with Shopify, we confirmed on October 23 that a third party obtained customer shipping information. You trusted us with those details, and we're sorry we didn't keep them safe.

Exposed: names, contact details, shipping addresses, and order details (items and prices).
Not exposed: payment card or bank details, recovery phrases, private keys, or wallet passwords.

We've blocked access, fixed the vulnerability, opened an investigation, and are emailing affected customers.

Scammers may pose as Keystone by phone, text, email, or mail, offering refunds, replacement devices, or "fixes" for your order or address. None of it is from us.

NEVER share your recovery phrase or private keys, and NEVER enter your recovery phrase into a device you didn't order. We will never ask for them. Don't click links in unexpected messages. Type https://t.co/7km8AZM288 yourself.

A detailed report is coming soon.

Until then, trust only our official channels. If anything feels off, email support@keyst.one. We'd rather hear from you than have you take a chance.

Again, we're truly sorry to everyone affected.

text:
The internet is coming out of LOCKDOWN.

“Black October” has seen MILLIONS of hacking attempts as two critical PHP flaws triggered emergency shutdowns across governments, banks and major platforms.

If these headlines have left you worried, there’s another part of the story you need to see.

As of October 23, no government or security firm had confirmed a single successful PHP2Shell attack.

Websites that went dark are coming back.

Wikipedia had outages during the scramble and was back up the next day.

US banks have dodged early damage too, per American Banker.

Here’s how the world is fighting BACK:

Cloudflare switched on protection hours before the official fix came out, even for free users.

PHP shipped fixes for both flaws on October 21, a day after details leaked.

Big hosts and clouds like Hostinger, Google and Amazon rolled out updates to the PHP they manage for customers.

Governments told site owners to patch or go offline.

Many shutdowns were deliberate precautions, giving operators time to install those fixes.

Getting the fixes onto every affected system is now the challenge.

Anyone managing a PHP server needs to confirm the fixes are installed.

A third, separate PHP issue disclosed on October 23 has a temporary workaround while its software fix is prepared.

That issue requires an unusual combination of settings and application behavior.

There is still no reliable worldwide count of websites that have finished patching.

Security firm NCC Group warns there’s “a real possibility” some vulnerable systems were already compromised.

For us, there are precautions worth taking now.

Secure your email with a unique password and enable passkeys or 2FA.

Replace any passwords you’ve reused across accounts.

Check official notices from services you use.

Check unexpected account warnings by opening the official app or website directly.

Keep your devices updated through official settings.

Never install a supposed “PHP patch” sent in a message.

Run a website? Check with your host that PHP itself is patched, since WordPress and plugins run on top of PHP and can’t fix it.

We don’t yet know what the coming months or ongoing investigations will reveal.

But fixes are being deployed, defenses are being strengthened and there are steps we can take today.

We can’t prevent every company breach, but we can make it harder for one breach to spread into the rest of our lives.
author: crypto_bitlord7
quoted_text:
The internet is going into a LOCKDOWN.

Hundreds of millions of websites are potentially at risk from cyberattacks.

Governments, banks and major platforms have already taken their websites OFFLINE.

Many are already calling it “Black October.”

At the centre of the shutdowns is something most of us have never heard of, but use every day.

PHP, the software behind roughly 7 in 10 websites, has two critical flaws that can let hackers break in without a password.

Dubbed PHP2Shell, both are rated 9.2 out of 10 for severity.

Details began circulating on Oct 20. Emergency fixes arrived the next day, but attackers were already moving.

Cloudflare’s CEO says hacking attempts then jumped from thousands to MILLIONS within hours.

Cybersecurity agencies across several countries are telling PHP site owners the same thing: Patch it now, or take it offline.

Websites have gone dark worldwide, from government portals and hospitals to banks.

CrowdStrike warns these attacks leave almost no trace, so some sites may not know if they’ve been hit.

Around 2.6 MILLION internet-facing servers run PHP, potentially hosting hundreds of sites each.

Over 1.1 million use older versions no longer receiving official PHP updates.

Older installations may need an upgrade to a supported PHP version or a fix from their software provider.

And patching does not remove a backdoor an attacker may already have planted.

Cloudflare also says hackers are now tweaking their attacks to try to slip past its protections.

But PHP isn’t the only security story unfolding.

-Japan’s Onamae suspended ALL Desktop Cloud plans after malware was found on customer servers.

-India’s eMudhra had 8 website-certificate keys so weak, one was literally the number “4”.

-State Bank of India confirmed 3,897 customer records on the dark web.

-Criminals used AI agents to break into 400+ Latin American banks.

-Capcom confirmed a breach exposing 11.7 million email addresses.

-GitLab disclosed a 10/10 severity flaw in versions going back to 2014.

-LiteLLM removed a malware-containing release. Railway reported possible exposure of customer secrets.

None of these has a confirmed link to PHP2Shell.

We’re seeing separate breaches unfold together.

The true number of incidents could take months to come out.

The world is still on alert. Attacks are still coming.

One year in at @katana . It's been a ride.

This past year has been one of the most intense and rewarding periods of growth for me, both on the business side and as a developer.

What started as a Developer Relations role evolved into so much more. I've had the opportunity to contribute across product, marketing, AI optimization, community, engineering, and feature design.

But the dev in me never stopped getting my hands dirty on the technical side.

I've built and operated liquidation bots, perps trading bots, AI-driven delta-neutral strategy bots, and arbitrage bots (still haven't figured out how to make that arbitrage profitable, lmao).

One of the biggest takeaways, though, has been the people I've worked alongside.

We're a tight team and I've learned something from every single person.

The Katana Perps team are true OGs. Watching their meticulous approach to engineering, optimization, and execution has been an education in itself. When a team has worked together for over seven years, you can see it in how they operate, solve problems, and build. That kind of chemistry is hard to replicate.

It's been intense. My socials haven't been nearly as active as they used to be, but that's because I've been heads down, building, experimenting, learning, and constantly pushing myself to improve.

One year in, and I still feel like there's so much more to learn and build.

text:
马斯克说：“未来金钱将失去意义。”
奥特曼反手一刀：“埃隆想多了，10年后钱依然重要得很。”

奥特曼的意思其实很露骨：
1 物质通缩？同意。 AI确实会让商品、服务和算力成本雪崩。

2 消灭金钱？扯淡。 成本跌了不等于免费，更不等于大家都能躺平。

3 核心恐慌是“阶级固化”： 奥特曼直言，AI最危险的不是产生意识，而是技术与资本极度集中在极少数人手里。AI不会自动消灭贫富差距，只会像杠杆一样把它撬得更夸张。

4 至于人类会不会被灭？ 奥特曼秒答：“概率极低。”

埃隆聊的是50年后的终极幻想，奥特曼算的是未来10年的资产负债表。

现实是：生产要素可能归零，但稀缺性永远存在。未来拉开人与人之间差距的，不再是勤奋，而是你究竟是在消费AI，还是在用AI构建资产。

你站马斯克的乌托邦，还是奥特曼的现实主义？

On 22nd October, Holy Mother Church celebrates Pope Saint John Paul II’s optional Memorial, which marks his installation Mass to the Papacy on 22 October 1978.

In his first homily of his papacy, he aptly captured the cultural despair of a post-Christian world, and pointed to the antidote: 

“So often today man does not know what is within him, in the depths of his mind and heart. So often he is uncertain about the meaning of his life on this earth. He is assailed by doubt, a doubt which turns into despair. We ask you therefore, we beg you with humility and trust, let Christ speak to man. He alone has words of life, yes, of eternal life.”

Throughout his life, John Paul II fought back against a world broken by fear and despair. His life and legacy exist as a great refutation of Satan’s lies and fear mongering. Notably however, he did not dwell frequently on the enemy in his words, though he was always aware of the threat. Instead, with unwavering faith in the Resurrection, he lived his life in tremendous joy, even through his long years of suffering and illness.

John Paul II encourages us to, like the first disciples, follow Jesus! To not be afraid to draw near to Him, to cross the threshold of His dwelling, to speak with Him, face to face, as you talk with a friend (cf. Ex 33:11). To not be afraid of the “new life” He is offering. He Himself makes it possible

text:
Three arms, one island

The Celts swore their oaths by three things: unless the sky falls, unless the sea breaks its bounds, unless the earth opens beneath us. Three realms, held together by a promise.

Their sign for it turns: the triskele, three arms spinning from one centre. On the Isle of Man it is still the flag, and legend says it is the sea god Manannán himself, rolling across the mist on three legs. An island in the middle of the sea, wearing three arms.

And their Otherworld was always an island across the water. The Isle of Apples. The Land of Youth. Hy-Brasil, seen once in seven years. The kingdom under the wave. Ys, Lyonesse, the drowned lands their bards would not forget.

Inside Newgrange, older than any Celt, the triple spiral is cut in the dark. The Celts inherited it and made the mound a home of gods.

In Ethiopia that sign is a landscape.

The upper water: the springs and lakes of the highland plateau, 2,500 metres up, where the river is born. The heavens’ water, falling and gathered.

The middle water: the Awash, descending through its valley, twelve stations from the plateau to the plain. The living river, the water that walks.

The lower water: the salt. The depression sinks below the level of the sea, and there the river never reaches the ocean. It dies into the terminal lakes, into brine, into the underworld laid bare.

Three waters, three worlds, stacked one above the other in rock and air. And where do they meet?

At one point only: the island in the terminal lake, where the waters of the plateau arrive by the river and stand still above the salt.

The centre the three arms turn around, a centre that held everything around it. The triskelion is the same idea drawn in one line: three worlds, one hub.

#Atlantis #CelticMythology #Triskelion

text:
*Post 1/12*  
I CANCELLED MY FUNERAL™  
CHAPTER 2: BARN, BLOOD, STARS  
by Ulyssesfve2™  

I came out of the barn dirty with blood 4:50am. Knife still in my hand. The air was cold, and the only sound was my own breathing and the drip of something I didn’t want to look at.  
I didn’t wipe it off. Didn’t care.  
I looked up at the stars and pointed the knife right at them.  
“Nothing’s gonna stop humanity from taking you,” I said. Stupid? Maybe 

*Post 2/12*  
I pointed that knife at the stars and made the promise like it was a contract.  
“Nothing’s gonna stop humanity from getting up there.”  
And I meant it.  
Not because I’d read it somewhere.  
I meant it because I was standing there, blood on my hands, pocket heavy with money I actually earned.  
From nothing.  
Building housing, climbing out of nowhere, sleeping in places you wouldn’t park a car.

*Post 3/12*  
If a guy like me could make it that far, then what’s stopping the rest of us?  
I felt it in my chest — the invisibility of the human spirit.  
How it bends but doesn’t break.  
My pocket was heavy. Coins and notes stuffed in the inside of my jacket, pressing against my ribs.  
Cash in hand, no bank, no mortgage, no 25 years of interest eating you alive.

*Post 4/12*  
Right in front of me was Baldur.  
The finest bull this area ever produced.  
He ran at me from the fields the way he always did, expecting feed, expecting me.  
I had to slaughter him.  
It’s not clean. The knife has to find the exact spot, and you have to commit. The blood came hot, fast, and it soaked into the dirt, into my boots.

*Post 5/12*  
There’s a smell to it — iron and earth and something primal that sticks in your nose for days.  
Money in the pocket, blood on the hands.And the worst part? It made sense.I was there when Baldur was born.
*3 AM*, freezing, cow on her side bawling, and me with my arm elbow-deep trying to turn him right so he wouldn’t die.

*Post 6/12*  
For the next 2 years I fed him, checked him, knew his limp before the vet did.  You name them even when you tell yourself not to.  
You talk to them when it’s 2 AM and you can’t sleep.But you’re not supposed to love livestock. That’s rule one. Love gets in the way of the ledger.

*Post 7/12*  
And then the clients start queuing up.  Not people. Hyenas. Smiling, “When’s it ready? How much for the cut? Supermarket is cheaper.” I’m collecting the money, counting it, feeling the notes stick together with sweat.And every note feels like 30 pieces of silver.

*Post 8/12*  
Because I’m the one who raised him.  I’m the one he ran to.  
And I’m the one turning that trust into cash.  By the gate.  
Seven guys who’d followed me through winters with no heating, summers where we slept in half-built houses.  They didn’t say anything when they saw me.  
Blood on my jacket, knife still in my hand, Baldur’s body behind me steaming in the cold.

*Post 9/12*  
They knew.  Generosity makes people uncomfortable when they’re the ones benefiting.  
Give a man a bonus when he expects minimum wage, and for 10 seconds he’s grateful.  After that, he starts wondering what you want from him.  But they still would’ve followed me to hell.  Because I’d bled with them.

*Post 10/12*  
The crew was quiet because they were already doing the math.  
About me.  When you stand there with cash in your pocket and a dead animal at your feet, people stop seeing a man.  They see a resource.  A faucet.  A threat.

*Post 11/12*  
The guy who’d carry you out of a fire yesterday is now wondering if you’ll cut his pay tomorrow.  
You understand that “human nature” isn’t about love and struggle.  It’s survival dressed up in morality.  People love you for what you give, hate you for what you keep, and betray you the second it costs them nothing.

*Post 12/12*  
I stood there and I asked, "God, what have I become?"
This is why men go quiet.  
End of Chapter 2
